AI.result: On ABC, Fusion360, NIST and DeepCAD, DecompRL achieves the highest success rate among the evaluated learning-based methods on three of the four benchmarks, while keeping mesh quality competitive. The largest success-rate improvement is on Fusion360, where it reaches 59.6%. The LMFF-to-DecompRL runtime ratio reaches up to two orders of magnitude, but this compares decomposition alone, excluding mesh generation.
AI.conclusion: Internal splitting actions combined with meshability feedback produce more valid decompositions for hexahedral meshing, with the clearest gain on the Fusion360 benchmark.

title: A Unified Interactive Framework for Real-Time Three-Dimensional Cellular Automata Simulation in XR
summary: Integrating three-dimensional cellular automata (3D CA) into extended reality (XR) requires coordinated simulation, volumetric data management, rendering, and interaction under variable hardware constraints. This paper presents a hybrid study combining a critical review of existing approaches with a unified architecture for real-time 3D CA in XR. The proposed five-layer architecture integrates voxel and rule management, parallel computation, interoperability middleware, visualization, and XR interaction. Its key principles include hardware-aware execution, asynchronous simulation-rendering, adaptive fidelity, and cross-engine interoperability. An analytical evaluation framework is defined to assess performance, latency, scalability, memory efficiency, simulation correctness, and interaction quality. The proposed framework provides a foundation for developing portable and interactive 3D CA systems across desktop and mobile XR platforms.

AI.tldr: Presents a hybrid review and a five-layer unified architecture for real-time three-dimensional cellular automata simulation in XR, together with an analytical evaluation framework; the abstract reports no measured results.
AI.motivation: Integrating 3D cellular automata into XR requires coordinated simulation, volumetric data management, rendering and interaction under variable hardware constraints, and the paper critically reviews existing approaches to address this.
AI.method: The five-layer architecture integrates voxel and rule management, parallel computation, interoperability middleware, visualization and XR interaction. Its principles are hardware-aware execution, asynchronous simulation-rendering, adaptive fidelity and cross-engine interoperability. An analytical evaluation framework is defined for performance, latency, scalability, memory efficiency, simulation correctness and interaction quality.
AI.result: The evaluation framework is defined analytically; the abstract reports no experimental measurements or comparisons.
AI.conclusion: The framework is offered as a foundation for developing portable and interactive 3D cellular automata systems across desktop and mobile XR platforms.

title: Deformable Texture Maps: Compiling Dynamic Microgeometry into Neural Textures
summary: Deformable material surfaces, such as cloth, owe their appearance to fine-scale geometries that restructure under deformation. Even when coarse simulation models efficiently recover this microstructure, explicitly instantiating and rendering it remains expensive. We introduce Deformable Texture Maps (DTM), a representation that compiles deformation-driven microgeometry into a continuous and compact neural texture. Our model maps texture coordinates and local deformations to intrinsic maps describing opacity, surface normals, depth, and material identity. This captures the occlusion and visibility changes generated by deformation. At runtime, these maps provide a common texture-space representation of deformation-driven fine-scale structure that can be evaluated directly on coarse deforming surfaces. Since our representation encodes geometric attributes rather than radiance, lighting and material response remain decoupled from the learned model. This allows us to apply relighting, as well as shading and material editing without retraining. We further introduce a persistent texture-space rendering strategy that caches these intrinsic maps and selectively updates them as deformation changes. This effectively decouples neural evaluation from frame rendering and enables their reuse across frames and conventional rendering effects. We demonstrate our approach on yarn-based textiles, where non-linear material stretch and shear induce changes in yarn geometry, spacing and occlusion. We build our model by, first, sweeping tileable yarn patches through deformation space, then, rendering the detailed geometry into a canonical texture-space, and finally, compressing the resulting maps into a single neural representation. Our resulting model can be evaluated directly on arbitrary coarse garment meshes and integrated with conventional shading pipelines, keeping appearance authorable at render time.

AI.tldr: Introduces Deformable Texture Maps, a compact neural texture that encodes deformation-driven microgeometry as opacity, normal, depth and material maps, and evaluates them directly on coarse deforming meshes such as yarn-based garments.
AI.motivation: Explicitly instantiating and rendering the fine-scale microstructure of deforming materials such as cloth is expensive, even when coarse simulation models can recover that microstructure efficiently.
AI.method: A neural model maps texture coordinates and local deformations to intrinsic maps. Tileable yarn patches are swept through deformation space, rendered into a canonical texture space, and compressed into a single neural representation. A persistent texture-space rendering strategy caches the intrinsic maps and selectively updates them as deformation changes.
AI.result: Because the representation encodes geometric attributes rather than radiance, relighting, shading and material editing can be applied without retraining. The model can be evaluated directly on arbitrary coarse garment meshes and integrated with conventional shading pipelines. The abstract reports no quantitative benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Encoding geometry rather than radiance and decoupling neural evaluation from frame rendering keeps the appearance of deforming textiles authorable at render time.

title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
summary: We present FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control. FAME-QP combines constraint-dependent operator representations with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs, automatically selecting the execution configuration through device calibration and problem-specific timing. It probes a cached operator bank to select the initial penalty and updates operators lazily when problem matrices change. Numerical benchmarks and simulated humanoid and quadrotor control experiments demonstrate reduced latency relative to competing GPU solvers while maintaining solution accuracy and control performance.

AI.tldr: Presents FAME-QP, a GPU solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control, using fused kernels replayed through CUDA graphs, automatic execution configuration and a cached operator bank.
AI.motivation: Real-time linear model predictive control needs fast solutions of dense quadratic programs, and the paper targets lower latency than competing GPU solvers.
AI.method: Constraint-dependent operator representations are combined with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs. The execution configuration is chosen automatically from device calibration and problem-specific timing. A cached operator bank selects the initial penalty, and operators are updated lazily when problem matrices change.
AI.result: Numerical benchmarks and simulated humanoid and quadrotor control experiments show reduced latency relative to competing GPU solvers while maintaining solution accuracy and control performance. The abstract gives no specific speedup figures.
AI.conclusion: The solver offers a GPU route to lower-latency MPC for robotic control without sacrificing solution accuracy or control performance, according to the reported experiments.

title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
summary: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$. A graph has strict level $k$ if it admits a reduction at level $k$ and none at level $k-1$. For every $k\geq1$, we construct a graph of strict level $k$ with $3k+8$ vertices. Each step adds three vertices: the neighbours of one induce the preceding graph, and the other two provide the adjacencies used to rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order $4k+4$ at strict level $k$. Together the two families give the upper bound $\min\{4k+4,3k+8\}$ on the least order at strict level $k$.

AI.tldr: Constructs graphs at every strict dismantling level k, with 3k+8 vertices in one family and 4k+4 vertices in another, giving the upper bound min{4k+4, 3k+8} on the least order of a graph of strict level k.
AI.motivation: Dismantling is defined recursively, so level-k eligibility requires the neighbourhood of a vertex to be dismantlable at level k-1; the minimum order of a graph of strict level k needs explicit constructions to bound it.
AI.method: Each step of the first construction adds three vertices, so that the neighbours of one vertex induce the preceding graph while the other two vertices supply adjacencies that rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order 4k+4 at strict level k.
AI.result: For every k at least 1 there is a graph of strict level k with 3k+8 vertices, and a second family of order 4k+4, which together yield the bound min{4k+4, 3k+8}.
AI.conclusion: Linear-size graphs suffice at every strict level, so the least order grows at most linearly in k; the abstract gives no matching lower bound.

title: A Lightweight Differentiable Method for Real-Time Skin Rendering and Digitization
comment: 20 pages, 25 figures; includes 6 pages of supplementary material. Accepted to Computers and Graphics
summary: Inverse rendering for skin typically relies on offline path tracing to estimate physical properties, which fail to map directly to the approximate shaders utilized in interactive applications, such as game engines. We bridge this gap by directly estimating subsurface scattering parameters tailored for real-time rendering pipelines. We introduce a differentiable Screen-Space Subsurface Scattering (SSSS) framework that enables the joint optimization of spatially varying base textures and scattering distances. To account for local variations in skin thickness, we estimate these parameters across distinct facial regions, generating a blended profile map ready for production runtime engines. Our pipeline utilizes a low-cost, single-light, single-view capture setup designed for accessible and practical appearance acquisition. Optimization is driven by a masked loss function targeting regions where subsurface scattering effects are dominant. We validate our approach on a real-world dataset of $45$ individuals across the Monk Skin Tone Scale, ensuring demographic generalization. Furthermore, we complement this evaluation with synthetic data, a multi-light setup validating our single-light assumption, and a tilted-view configuration confirming angular consistency. Results demonstrate that our method effectively recovers scattering parameters from lightweight inputs, yielding realistic skin appearance directly compatible with standard real-time shaders.

AI.tldr: Proposes a differentiable screen-space subsurface scattering framework that estimates skin scattering parameters and base textures for real-time shaders from a low-cost, single-light, single-view capture.
AI.motivation: Inverse rendering for skin usually relies on offline path tracing, whose estimated physical properties do not map directly to the approximate shaders used in interactive applications such as game engines.
AI.method: Spatially varying base textures and scattering distances are jointly optimized in a differentiable screen-space subsurface scattering (SSSS) framework. Parameters are estimated per facial region to produce a blended profile map, and a masked loss targets regions where subsurface scattering dominates.
AI.result: The method is validated on a real dataset of 45 individuals across the Monk Skin Tone Scale, with synthetic data, a multi-light setup checking the single-light assumption and a tilted-view configuration checking angular consistency. The recovered parameters yield realistic skin appearance compatible with standard real-time shaders.
AI.conclusion: Lightweight capture is enough to recover scattering parameters that run directly in production real-time shaders across a range of skin tones.

title: Uncovering the Blind Spots of OKS-mAP: A Unified Protocol for Occlusion, Joint-Angle, and Temporal Evaluation of 2D Pose Estimators
summary: The dominant metric for 2D human pose estimation, OKS-mAP, has three blind spots: it does not distinguish visible from occluded keypoints, does not measure joint-angle error, and is silent on the temporal stability of tracking-free per-frame inference. We propose a supplementary protocol with three modules: (M1) OKS-mAP stratified by ground-truth visibility, with Delta_occ = mAP(v=1) - mAP(full), quantifying how much the aggregate metric masks occlusion-specific differences; (M2) joint-angle error (RMSE/MAE/P95) plus knee-valgus detection consistency; (M3) frame-to-frame displacement, median-filter residual jitter, and jump rate, before and after OneEuro smoothing. We ran it on four datasets (COCO val2017, CrowdPose, OCHuman, PoseTrack18) and four models from two architecture families (YOLO11s-pose, an occlusion-domain fine-tuned variant, ViTPose-B/L), under a common detector-free oracle protocol and an open-source harness. Delta_occ is negative in every combination (-0.19 to -0.47): aggregate mAP overestimates occluded-scene performance in every tested combination. Joint-angle error is amplified in occluded layers; angle metrics reveal differences mAP cannot localize, e.g., the smaller occlusion-trained model significantly outperforming a larger transformer in occluded elbows. On PoseTrack18 val, raw jitter matched between the two YOLO models; pixel-domain OneEuro smoothing cut jump rates 9-10% at no matched-scope AP cost; residual jitter persists after detector removal; the transformer pair's jump rate is significantly lower; smoothing benefits replicate across architectures. Stratified mAP tracks full mAP closely (sign-consistency 1.0, 12/12), serving magnitude diagnosis rather than re-ranking; angle-metric difference vectors (especially knee) partially diverge, suggesting independent information. The protocol and harness are open-sourced, complementing rather than replacing OKS-mAP.

AI.tldr: Proposes a supplementary evaluation protocol for 2D pose estimators with three modules (visibility-stratified OKS-mAP, joint-angle error, and temporal jitter and jump metrics), and finds that aggregate mAP overestimates occluded-scene performance in every tested combination.
AI.motivation: OKS-mAP does not distinguish visible from occluded keypoints, does not measure joint-angle error, and says nothing about the temporal stability of tracking-free per-frame inference.
AI.method: M1 stratifies OKS-mAP by ground-truth visibility and defines Delta_occ = mAP(v=1) - mAP(full). M2 reports joint-angle RMSE, MAE and P95 together with knee-valgus detection consistency. M3 measures frame-to-frame displacement, median-filter residual jitter and jump rate before and after OneEuro smoothing. It is run on COCO val2017, CrowdPose, OCHuman and PoseTrack18 with four models from two architecture families under a detector-free oracle protocol.
AI.result: Delta_occ is negative in every combination, from -0.19 to -0.47. Joint-angle error is amplified in occluded layers, and a smaller occlusion-trained model significantly outperforms a larger transformer on occluded elbows. OneEuro smoothing cuts jump rates by 9-10% at no matched-scope AP cost, and the benefit replicates across architectures. Stratified mAP tracks full mAP closely (sign-consistency 1.0, 12/12).
AI.conclusion: The protocol complements rather than replaces OKS-mAP, adding occlusion, angle and temporal diagnostics that the aggregate metric cannot localize, and the protocol and harness are open-sourced.

title: URL-Sim: Unified and Regulated LiDAR Simulation for High-Fidelity Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes
summary: Reconstructing high-fidelity LiDAR simulation scenes from real-world driving logs is essential for cost-effective safety validation of autonomous driving systems. While simulators based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) achieve realistic scene reconstruction, their large-scale adoption is limited by slow rendering speeds. Recent 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) approaches have improved rendering efficiency through explicit primitive representation and differentiable rasterization. However, existing 3DGS-based methods remain largely restricted to rigid vehicles and produce redundant primitives through unconstrained densification. To address these limitations, we propose URL-Sim, a unified and regulated dynamic LiDAR simulation framework. URL-Sim constructs a dynamic Gaussian scene graph that decouples the modeling of traffic participants, including vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists, enabling accurate reconstruction of heterogeneous dynamic objects within a single framework. It further introduces a regulated Gaussian densification strategy that ranks primitives with multi-dimensional importance scores and allocates Gaussians to the most critical regions while keeping the total primitive count bounded. Experiments on the Waymo and KITTI-360 datasets demonstrate that URL-Sim achieves higher quantitative accuracy and visual quality than existing baselines under comparable primitive budgets, and accurately recovers the geometry and poses of diverse dynamic traffic participants.

AI.tldr: Proposes URL-Sim, a dynamic LiDAR simulation framework that uses a Gaussian scene graph to model vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists, and a regulated densification strategy that keeps the total primitive count bounded.
AI.motivation: NeRF-based LiDAR simulators render slowly, and existing 3DGS methods are largely restricted to rigid vehicles and produce redundant primitives through unconstrained densification.
AI.method: A dynamic Gaussian scene graph decouples traffic participants so that heterogeneous dynamic objects are reconstructed within one framework. The regulated densification strategy ranks primitives by multi-dimensional importance scores and allocates Gaussians to the most critical regions while keeping the total count bounded.
AI.result: On the Waymo and KITTI-360 datasets, URL-Sim achieves higher quantitative accuracy and visual quality than existing baselines under comparable primitive budgets, and accurately recovers the geometry and poses of diverse dynamic traffic participants.
AI.conclusion: Decoupled scene graphs and budgeted densification extend 3DGS-based LiDAR reconstruction beyond rigid vehicles while keeping primitive counts bounded.

title: Evaluation protocols for historical script classification: the cost of manuscript-level leakage and the role of soft labels
summary: A paleographer applies a script type classifier to unseen manuscripts. We measure how much testing on other pages of training manuscripts inflates accuracy. On VML-HP-ext (715 pages, 171 Hebrew manuscripts, 14 script classes) we compare page-level and manuscript-level splits. Page-level accuracy drops from 97% to 54% (59% at manuscript level), and is 39% on the official blind test set. The gap of 40 to 47 percentage points (pp) at patch, page and manuscript level is statistically significant and reproduces with ResNet18; on binarized patches (ink and background only) it is 34 to 42 pp, also significant. On unseen manuscripts the model is overconfident: mean confidence 70% against 54% correct pages; patch-level expected calibration error (ECE, mean gap between confidence and accuracy) rises from 0.065 to 0.444. Binarization leaves patch-level overconfidence but cuts it markedly at page level. Confidence still helps triage: in the more confident half of pages 67% are correct, 41% in the rest. Training on expert soft labels showed no evidence of an accuracy difference, though a small page-level loss cannot be ruled out. The predicted distributions are closer to the expert's assessment. ECE is lower at patch level (0.21 to 0.31) and in most runs at page level, but not significantly at manuscript level. Label smoothing (blurring the label, no expert input) also lowers ECE but comes no closer to the expert. Temperature scaling (post-training confidence correction) helps significantly only at patch level. On 97 pages of 16 manuscripts with mixed expert assessment, soft labels cut divergence from the expert by 22 to 30% (significant in four of five runs); the point estimate of accuracy is 16.5 to 23.7 pp below hard labels, but with 16 manuscripts the loss can neither be confirmed nor ruled out. We propose recommendations for the evaluation protocol; code will be released with the paper

AI.tldr: Shows that testing a historical script classifier on other pages of training manuscripts inflates accuracy, with page-level accuracy of 97% falling to 54% under manuscript-level splits, and that the model is overconfident on unseen manuscripts; soft expert labels show no evidence of an accuracy difference but bring predictions closer to the expert.
AI.motivation: A paleographer applies a script type classifier to unseen manuscripts, but evaluation that tests on other pages of training manuscripts may overstate how well the classifier generalizes.
AI.method: On VML-HP-ext (715 pages, 171 Hebrew manuscripts, 14 script classes), page-level and manuscript-level splits are compared at patch, page and manuscript level. The study replicates with ResNet18, repeats the comparison on binarized patches, analyses calibration (ECE, temperature scaling, label smoothing), and trains on expert soft labels evaluated on 97 pages of 16 manuscripts with mixed expert assessment.
AI.result: The 40 to 47 percentage point gap between split protocols is significant and reproduces with ResNet18; on binarized patches it is 34 to 42 points. Accuracy is 39% on the official blind test set. On unseen manuscripts the model is overconfident (mean confidence 70% against 54% correct pages), and patch-level ECE rises from 0.065 to 0.444. In the more confident half of pages 67% are correct, against 41% in the rest. Soft labels cut divergence from the expert by 22 to 30%, but their accuracy point estimate is 16.5 to 23.7 points below hard labels, a difference 16 manuscripts can neither confirm nor rule out.
AI.conclusion: Page-level evaluation overstates generalization to unseen manuscripts, so evaluation protocols should split by manuscript, and model confidence helps triage but is not reliably calibrated.

title: Attribute-Evidence Learning with Multimodal Prompt for Generalized Category Discovery
comment: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI)
summary: Generalized category discovery (GCD) aims to discover novel categories from unlabeled data by leveraging limited labeled samples from old classes. Existing methods that rely solely on visual cues often neglect the multimodal nature of human perception, prompting recent approaches to incorporate textual information such as category tags and attributes. However, these approaches typically entangle global tags and local attributes within a shared global image representation, rendering attributes unreliable and potentially providing misleading cues that can drive the model toward incorrect predictions. To this end, we propose AptM-GCD, a novel multimodal framework that exploits apt textual guidance through attribute evidence learning and multimodal prompt reasoning. Specifically, we design an Attribute-Evidence Learning (AEL) mechanism that treats attributes as localized visual evidence rather than global category descriptors. By interacting attribute embeddings with patch-level visual tokens, AEL identifies reliable attribute-related regions and extracts discriminative local evidence, thereby reducing the impact of noisy or irrelevant attribute cues. Building upon the extracted evidence, we further develop a Multimodal Prompt Learning (MPL) mechanism to bridge local attribute semantics and global visual understanding. MPL converts fine-grained textual evidence into visual prompts and injects them into a multimodal prompt transformer, enabling attribute information to enhance category discrimination through contextual reasoning without enforcing direct global alignment between modalities. Extensive experiments on six datasets demonstrate that AptM-GCD consistently achieves SoTA performance across both fine-grained and generic benchmarks. Moreover, the proposed framework exhibits strong generalization ability, delivering consistent gains under unimodal and class-imbalanced GCD settings.

AI.tldr: Proposes AptM-GCD, which treats textual attributes as localized visual evidence and injects that evidence as prompts into a multimodal prompt transformer, reporting state-of-the-art performance on six datasets for generalized category discovery.
AI.motivation: Visual-only generalized category discovery ignores the multimodal nature of perception, while existing text-augmented methods entangle global tags and local attributes in one shared global image representation, which makes attributes unreliable and can mislead predictions.
AI.method: An Attribute-Evidence Learning mechanism interacts attribute embeddings with patch-level visual tokens to find attribute-related regions and extract discriminative local evidence. A Multimodal Prompt Learning mechanism converts this evidence into visual prompts injected into a multimodal prompt transformer, without enforcing direct global alignment between the modalities.
AI.result: AptM-GCD consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance across fine-grained and generic benchmarks on six datasets, and gives consistent gains under unimodal and class-imbalanced GCD settings.
AI.conclusion: Treating attributes as localized evidence rather than global category descriptors makes textual guidance reliable enough to help discover novel categories.

title: Partition, Refine, and Detect: Preserving Novel Category Capacity in Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
summary: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) expects the model trained on base classes to recognize both base and novel classes at inference. Typical methods rely on CLIP-style vision-language embeddings, yet the learned space is often biased toward base categories, with limited effective capacity preserved for novel concepts. Such a base-dominated representation can compress novel semantics, leading to semantic collapse and mis-calibrated confidence at inference. To address this issue, we present PR-OVD, a partition-and-refine framework that explicitly reserves capacity for novel categories and strengthens category separation, while being seamlessly integrated into different detector architectures. Specifically, PR-OVD first performs coarse partitioning to build global divisions for base, novel, and an explicit background partition in both visual and textual modalities, preventing object-irrelevant embeddings from leaking into category-specific representations. It then applies category-level refinement within each partition to sharpen decision boundaries and alleviate the lack of fine-grained region-level pretraining in CLIP. To further provide reliable visual anchors for novel categories, we design a cognitively inspired Structure Prompt (SP) that encodes both egocentric attributes and allocentric context, facilitating stable partition-and-refine learning. Extensive experiments on two OVD benchmarks show that PR-OVD delivers an average 6.5\% proportional improvement on novel categories over the state-of-the-art methods. Notably, PR-OVD also benefits other open-vocabulary tasks, including segmentation and classification, further confirming its effectiveness and generality.

AI.tldr: Proposes PR-OVD, a partition-and-refine framework that reserves capacity for novel categories in CLIP-based open-vocabulary object detection by partitioning base, novel and background embeddings and refining each partition, with an average 6.5% proportional improvement on novel categories.
AI.motivation: CLIP-style vision-language embeddings in open-vocabulary detection are biased toward base categories, which compresses novel semantics and leads to semantic collapse and mis-calibrated confidence at inference.
AI.method: Coarse partitioning builds base, novel and explicit background partitions in both visual and textual modalities, so that object-irrelevant embeddings do not leak into category-specific representations. Category-level refinement sharpens decision boundaries within each partition. A cognitively inspired Structure Prompt encodes egocentric attributes and allocentric context as visual anchors for novel categories.
AI.result: On two open-vocabulary detection benchmarks, PR-OVD delivers an average 6.5% proportional improvement on novel categories over state-of-the-art methods. It also benefits open-vocabulary segmentation and classification.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly reserving capacity for novel categories and refining partitions is an effective and general enhancement that integrates into different detector architectures.

title: Selective Surgical Action-Center Localization:Retaining Localization Gains through Supervised Scoring
summary: Surgical action-center localization requires both an accurate reference point and a decision about whether to report it. When frames with and without a reportable center are mixed, the benefit of improved localization depends on which correct candidates survive selection. We present a selective localization pipeline combining heatmap and coordinate supervision with a logistic-regression scorer. The scorer learns to identify predictions with a reportable center and a localization error within a specified tolerance. The internal evaluation uses 5,000 frames from 50 surgical sources, five source-grouped folds and two random seeds. Matched locator and scoring comparisons track correct candidates and their rejection. At an 80% acceptance quota per source and a tolerance of 0.10 times the image diagonal, our method retains 46.08 correct outputs per 100 inputs. The baseline locator with the same scoring approach retains 44.20. The gain is 1.88 (descriptive 95% source-paired bootstrap interval, 0.94 to 2.79). Under entropy-based selection, increased rejection of correct predictions offsets the higher supply of correct predictions on average. For the coordinate-supervised locator, supervised scoring reduces these rejections from 6.15 to 2.99 per 100 inputs. Evaluating retained correct outputs reveals whether a selection rule preserves or erodes an improvement in localization.

AI.tldr: Proposes a selective surgical action-center localization pipeline in which a logistic-regression scorer learns to accept only predictions with a reportable center and a localization error within tolerance, retaining 46.08 correct outputs per 100 inputs against 44.20 for the baseline locator.
AI.motivation: When frames with and without a reportable center are mixed, the benefit of better localization depends on which correct candidates survive selection, and the selection rule can erode the gain.
AI.method: Heatmap and coordinate supervision are combined with a logistic-regression scorer. The internal evaluation uses 5,000 frames from 50 surgical sources, five source-grouped folds and two random seeds, at an 80% per-source acceptance quota and a tolerance of 0.10 times the image diagonal.
AI.result: The method retains 46.08 correct outputs per 100 inputs against 44.20 for the baseline locator with the same scoring, a gain of 1.88 (descriptive 95% source-paired bootstrap interval 0.94 to 2.79). Under entropy-based selection, increased rejection of correct predictions offsets the higher supply of correct predictions on average. For the coordinate-supervised locator, supervised scoring reduces rejections of correct predictions from 6.15 to 2.99 per 100 inputs.
AI.conclusion: Supervised scoring preserves localization gains under selective acceptance better than entropy-based selection, and selection rules should be judged by the correct outputs they retain.

title: Trajectory-Regularized Distribution Distillation for One-Step Generation
summary: Distilling flow matching models for one-step generation generally follows two paradigms. Trajectory alignment supervises the student with the teacher's probability flow ODE, but its performance degrades under very small sampling budgets. Distribution matching directly optimizes the generated distribution, but estimating its reverse Kullback-Leibler gradient typically requires a separate network to track the evolving student score. We propose trajectory-regularized distribution distillation (TRD), which combines distribution-level and trajectory-level supervision through a momentum-mixture policy predicted in a single student forward pass. This policy serves simultaneously as a one-step generator, an estimator of the student's marginal velocity that removes the need for a second trainable network in distribution matching, and a closed-form time-dependent velocity field supervised along the teacher ODE trajectory. Experiments on SANA-1.6B and Stable Diffusion 3.5 show that TRD outperforms representative consistency and distribution matching baselines in generation quality and training efficiency for both one-step and few-step generation, with a trade-off in sample diversity.

AI.tldr: TRD distills flow matching models into one-step generators by combining distribution-level matching with trajectory-level supervision in one student forward pass; it outperforms consistency and distribution matching baselines on SANA-1.6B and Stable Diffusion 3.5, with a trade-off in sample diversity.
AI.motivation: Trajectory alignment degrades under very small sampling budgets, while distribution matching needs a separate network to track the evolving student score to estimate the reverse KL gradient.
AI.method: A momentum-mixture policy predicted in a single student forward pass serves three roles: the one-step generator, an estimator of the student's marginal velocity that removes the second trainable network, and a closed-form time-dependent velocity field supervised along the teacher ODE trajectory.
AI.result: On SANA-1.6B and Stable Diffusion 3.5, TRD outperforms representative consistency and distribution matching baselines in generation quality and training efficiency for both one-step and few-step generation, with a trade-off in sample diversity.
AI.conclusion: Combining distribution-level and trajectory-level supervision in one policy gives an efficient one-step distillation method, at some cost in diversity.

title: Evidence-Grounded Iterative Reasoning for the Diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases
summary: Overlapping imaging manifestations complicate the differential diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases (DCLDs), while limited annotated data constrain supervised model development. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can integrate imaging and clinical information, but their diagnostic reasoning remains limited by incomplete volumetric perception and insufficient grounding in disease-specific evidence. We propose DCLDs-EIR, an evidence-grounded iterative reasoning framework coupling diagnostic hypothesis refinement with multimodal evidence acquisition and verification. Multiview renderings of predicted lung and cyst segmentations characterize global cyst distributions and initialize the differential diagnosis. Competing hypotheses guide axial CT inspection to identify local findings that, together with clinical context, inform retrieval from a disease-specific knowledge graph. Accumulated patient observations and retrieved knowledge are jointly assessed for diagnostic support and refutation to revise the diagnostic state. Updated hypotheses and unresolved distinctions guide subsequent inspection, forming a feedback loop between evidence acquisition and hypothesis verification. Multicenter evaluation demonstrates that DCLDs-EIR consistently improves diagnostic accuracy over baselines and enables traceable differential diagnosis through explicit links between diagnostic hypotheses, patient observations, and disease-specific knowledge.

AI.tldr: DCLDs-EIR is an evidence-grounded iterative reasoning framework for diagnosing diffuse cystic lung diseases with multimodal LLMs; in multicenter evaluation it consistently improves diagnostic accuracy over baselines and makes differential diagnoses traceable.
AI.motivation: Overlapping imaging manifestations complicate the differential diagnosis of diffuse cystic lung diseases and annotated data are limited; existing MLLMs have incomplete volumetric perception and weak grounding in disease-specific evidence.
AI.method: Multiview renderings of predicted lung and cyst segmentations initialize the differential diagnosis; competing hypotheses guide axial CT inspection and retrieval from a disease-specific knowledge graph; observations and retrieved knowledge are assessed for support and refutation, forming a feedback loop between evidence acquisition and hypothesis verification.
AI.result: Multicenter evaluation shows DCLDs-EIR consistently improves diagnostic accuracy over baselines; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Explicit links between diagnostic hypotheses, patient observations and disease-specific knowledge make the differential diagnosis traceable as well as more accurate.

title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption
summary: Multimodal (e.g. vision-language, in this work) attribution aims to interpret the models without access to ground-truth explanatory supervision. Existing multimodal attribution methods typically rely on paired modalities as proxy supervision, implicitly assuming that image-text pairs are semantically aligned. Information bottleneck (IB)-based attribution methods follow this general paradigm and instantiate it through a global sufficiency-compression objective. In realistic multimodal datasets, however, this assumption is frequently violated due to partial semantic misalignment and unreliable cross-modal correspondences. Through theoretical analysis, we show that, under such misalignment, information-bottleneck-based attribution objectives exhibit a structural limitation: by assuming equal reliability across all proxy supervision signals, they induce posterior over-contraction and forced explanations. To address this issue, we propose TIB, a sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck framework that adaptively modulates attribution strength according to cross-modal reliability, without assuming semantic alignment. Extensive experiments on controlled benchmarks and large-scale datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed approach, while also validating the identified failure mode.

AI.tldr: TIB is a sample-wise tempered information bottleneck for multimodal attribution that scales attribution strength by cross-modal reliability instead of assuming image-text pairs are semantically aligned.
AI.motivation: IB-based attribution methods use paired modalities as proxy supervision and assume alignment; under partial semantic misalignment, equal reliability across proxy signals causes posterior over-contraction and forced explanations.
AI.method: A sample-wise tempered information bottleneck that adaptively modulates attribution strength according to cross-modal reliability, without assuming semantic alignment.
AI.result: Experiments on controlled benchmarks and large-scale datasets show the approach is effective and validate the identified failure mode; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Attribution objectives should weight proxy supervision by reliability rather than treat every image-text pair as aligned.

title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
summary: Embodied Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are backbones for robotic planning and manipulation. However, for coordinate prediction in grounding tasks, existing architectures suffer from two distinct bottlenecks: discrete tokenization disrupts spatial continuity with high decoding latency, while standard point regression fails on multi-contact affordances and irregularly shaped targets. To resolve these challenges, we propose PhysMoE, introducing three core contributions: (1) sharing lower layers for multimodal context while routing upper layers to specialized spatial (pixel) and linguistic (text) experts by physical modality, eliminating gradient interference; (2) encoding each coordinate as a single token by reusing the visual encoder's learned positional embeddings, injecting 2D spatial priors to natively align coordinates with visual features and ease training; and (3) differentiable Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision on pointing, accommodating affordances and irregular geometries without costly mask decoders. Compared to the base model, PhysMoE achieves a 15.7% average gain and an 8.31x throughput speedup across 9 coordinate-based grounding benchmarks (trajectory, affordance, and localization), while preserving multimodal understanding and reasoning across 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.

AI.tldr: PhysMoE is an embodied VLM for spatial grounding that encodes each coordinate as a single token and uses SDF supervision on pointing; it gains 15.7% on average across nine grounding benchmarks with an 8.31x throughput speedup while keeping multimodal reasoning on 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Discrete tokenization of coordinates breaks spatial continuity and decodes slowly, while standard point regression fails on multi-contact affordances and irregularly shaped targets.
AI.method: Lower layers are shared for multimodal context and upper layers route to pixel and text experts by physical modality; each coordinate is a single token reusing the visual encoder's learned positional embeddings; differentiable signed distance field supervision on pointing replaces costly mask decoders.
AI.result: Compared with the base model, PhysMoE gains 15.7% on average and runs 8.31x faster in throughput across 9 coordinate-based grounding benchmarks, while preserving multimodal understanding and reasoning across 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Modality-decoupled experts, single-token coordinates and SDF supervision together give faster and more accurate spatial grounding without losing general multimodal ability.

title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
summary: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables \(32\times\) and even effective \(64\times\) compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance. Since larger groups introduce intra-group dependencies that must be modeled efficiently, we analyze their impact on inference latency and generation quality and introduce a semi-autoregressive decoder that combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling. With these designs, our highly compressed models perform competitively with leading models across five representative text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, DPG-Bench, PRISM, LongText-Bench, and Qwen-Image-Bench). At \(1024\times1024\) resolution, our model delivers a \(20\times\) speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models, generating each image in 2.5 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200. Together, these results show that highly compressed discrete representations can enable high-quality autoregressive generation at low latency.

AI.tldr: G-STAR is a spatial-group co-scaling framework for discrete autoregressive image generation that reaches 32x and effective 64x compression, and generates 1024x1024 images in 2.5 seconds on one NVIDIA H200, a 20x speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models.
AI.motivation: Long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity.
AI.method: Based on product quantization, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor under a fixed nominal information budget; a semi-autoregressive decoder combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling to handle intra-group dependencies.
AI.result: The highly compressed models perform competitively with leading models on GenEval, DPG-Bench, PRISM, LongText-Bench and Qwen-Image-Bench; at 1024x1024 resolution they give a 20x speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models, generating each image in 2.5 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200.
AI.conclusion: Highly compressed discrete representations can enable high-quality autoregressive generation at low latency.

title: Instance-preserving graded semantic reporting for surgical action triplets
summary: Complete-or-reject reporting of surgical action triplets can discard a correctly identified instrument and action when the target is uncertain. We introduce instance-preserving graded semantic reporting, which separates instance selection from the choice of semantic detail. Each selected instance retains its predicted mask and labels while hierarchical correctness scores guide instrument (I), instrument-verb (IV), or complete instrument-verb-target (IVT) reporting. The utility-increment rule DELTA weighs the expected gain from finer reporting against its error cost. We compare three decision rules on 5,641 test frames from eight surgical videos using fixed predictions and scores. At the 10% development calibration target, DELTA retains correct partial reports for 80.0% of candidates rejected by a matched complete-or-reject baseline (5,329/6,662). Adding IV increases source-normalized weighted correct-report yield by 19.13 to 23.13 per 100 frames across all three rules relative to separately recalibrated I/IVT controls. Weighted reporting risk changes by -0.77 to +1.01 percentage points, with complete correct-triplet counts unchanged or reduced. Graded reporting makes partial surgical predictions available as localized descriptions, with an explicit trade-off between report utility and completeness.

AI.tldr: Instance-preserving graded semantic reporting keeps correctly identified surgical instruments and actions as partial reports instead of rejecting whole triplets; at a 10% calibration target the DELTA rule retains correct partial reports for 80.0% of candidates a matched complete-or-reject baseline rejects.
AI.motivation: Complete-or-reject reporting of surgical action triplets discards a correctly identified instrument and action when the target is uncertain.
AI.method: Instance selection is separated from the choice of semantic detail; hierarchical correctness scores guide instrument (I), instrument-verb (IV) or complete instrument-verb-target (IVT) reporting; the utility-increment rule DELTA weighs the expected gain from finer reporting against its error cost; three decision rules are compared.
AI.result: On 5,641 test frames from eight surgical videos, DELTA retains correct partial reports for 80.0% (5,329 of 6,662) of candidates rejected by a matched complete-or-reject baseline; adding IV raises source-normalized weighted correct-report yield by 19.13 to 23.13 per 100 frames across all three rules, with weighted reporting risk changing by -0.77 to +1.01 percentage points and complete correct-triplet counts unchanged or reduced.
AI.conclusion: Graded reporting makes partial surgical predictions available as localized descriptions, with an explicit trade-off between report utility and completeness.

title: Preserving Cultural Records: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Visual-Prior Routing Network for Ancient Book Image Restoration
summary: Ancient books preserve invaluable cultural heritage, yet their images often suffer from complex degradations caused by long-term ageing, environmental exposure, and physical damage. Existing ancient book image restoration benchmarks are limited in scale and rely on simplified degradation simulations, which cannot fully represent real-world degradation patterns and restrict the generalization ability of restoration models. To address these challenges, we introduce AncBench, a large-scale synthetic paired benchmark containing 100K aligned clean-degraded image pairs. AncBench models realistic composite degradations through a comprehensive degradation pipeline that considers material ageing, paper texture variation, blur, staining, water-induced geometric distortion, and local occlusion. Furthermore, we propose AncRestore, a degradation-aware visual-prior routing network for ancient book image restoration. AncRestore first learns degradation representations from degraded images and then dynamically selects and integrates suitable visual priors according to different degradation characteristics. Guided by these degradation cues, a dynamic routing mechanism combines expert-wise and region-wise routing strategies adaptively adjusts the contribution of these priors across different regions, enabling the model to recover both global appearance and local text details. Extensive experiments show that AncRestore effectively suppresses composite degradations while preserving text structures and enhancing restoration quality against other methods, highlighting its application potential for intelligent ancient book image restoration in cultural heritage preservation.

AI.tldr: AncBench is a 100K-pair synthetic benchmark for ancient book image restoration with realistic composite degradations, and AncRestore, a degradation-aware visual-prior routing network, suppresses these degradations while preserving text structures.
AI.motivation: Existing ancient book restoration benchmarks are small and rely on simplified degradation simulations that do not represent real-world degradation patterns, which limits the generalization of restoration models.
AI.method: AncBench models material ageing, paper texture variation, blur, staining, water-induced geometric distortion and local occlusion; AncRestore learns degradation representations, selects and integrates visual priors accordingly, and uses dynamic routing that combines expert-wise and region-wise strategies to adjust prior contributions across regions.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show AncRestore effectively suppresses composite degradations, preserves text structures and enhances restoration quality compared with other methods; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: The work highlights the potential of degradation-aware visual-prior routing for intelligent ancient book restoration in cultural heritage preservation.

title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
summary: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. The best configuration achieves 70.9% overall accuracy in GTAVBench-AGI, yet aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. GTAGym also provides a scalable generator that samples task parameters within user-specified ranges and option sets under fixed templates, creating batches of 3D and image-based shooting environments for RL with automatic reward and termination signals. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

AI.tldr: GTAGym is an environment and framework for evaluation and reinforcement learning on GTA V tasks; the best configuration reaches 70.9% overall accuracy on the harder GTAVBench-AGI branch, and LoRA RL on generated on-foot navigation tasks raises native GTA V task performance from 15% to 23%.
AI.motivation: Task outcomes in AAA games are hard to verify automatically and are often human-annotated, which also blocks reinforcement learning in these environments.
AI.method: GTAVBench has 103 online tasks across nine task families plus 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks, served through a web server with screenshot and keyboard-mouse actions and automatic engine-state outcome checks; GTAVBench-AGI shows instructions only in the first screenshot and compresses interaction history automatically; a generator samples task parameters for RL with automatic reward and termination signals.
AI.result: Six frontier LLMs were evaluated; the best configuration reaches 70.9% overall accuracy on GTAVBench-AGI, while aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves in-domain performance, transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and raises native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.
AI.conclusion: GTA V offers a scalable testbed for evaluating and training agents, and several task categories remain hard for frontier LLMs.

title: MICRO: A Surgery-Phase Retinal Image Rigid Registration Benchmark and One-Step Frequency-Structure Similarity Registration Learning
summary: Precise multimodal retinal image rigid registration (MRIRG) is essential for aligning cross-modal vessel structures, offering critical guidance for ophthalmic surgery. Despite its significance, the advancement of MRIRG is hindered by the lack of publicly available multimodal retinal image rigid registration datasets spanning various ophthalmic surgery phases (e.g., preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative). To address this issue, we introduce the MICRO dataset, a large-scale MRIRG benchmark, comprising 1,365 cross-modal retinal image pairs with standardized annotations across all ophthalmic surgery phases. Moreover, existing deep registration methods achieve competitive MRIRG results via a two-step segmentation-then-detection framework, but segmentation quality heavily constrains their performance. We argue that this dependency stems from an implicit need for keypoint topology constraints, which have not been exploited for MRIRG through a one-step registration framework. Inspired by the above analysis, we propose a novel One-step Frequency-Structure Similarity Registration (OFS2Reg) learning framework for MRIRG that leverages the potential of cross-modal vessel structure similarities to construct keypoint topology constraints under a shared detection network. To be specific, OFS2Reg applies a well-designed frequency-guided structure preservation descriptor to construct coarse keypoint topology constraints in descriptors by highlighting significant vessel structures. Additionally, we develop a new cross-modal vessel structure similarity learning method that refines cross-modal keypoint topology constraints to precisely align pixel-level cross-modal vessel structures by leveraging cross-modal vessel structure similarity priors.

AI.tldr: MICRO is a benchmark of 1,365 cross-modal retinal image pairs for surgery-phase rigid registration, and OFS2Reg is a one-step registration framework that uses keypoint topology constraints instead of a two-step segmentation-then-detection pipeline.
AI.motivation: Public multimodal retinal registration datasets covering all ophthalmic surgery phases are lacking, and two-step segmentation-then-detection methods depend heavily on segmentation quality.
AI.method: OFS2Reg uses a frequency-guided structure preservation descriptor to build coarse keypoint topology constraints under a shared detection network, and a cross-modal vessel structure similarity learning method that refines these constraints using similarity priors to align pixel-level vessel structures.
AI.result: The abstract reports no numerical results.
AI.conclusion: Exploiting cross-modal vessel structure similarity inside a one-step framework offers a route to registration that does not depend on segmentation quality.

title: SpatialSR: Spatial Resolution-Centric Pipeline for Arbitrary-Scale Remote Sensing Super-Resolution
summary: Although remote sensing image arbitrary-scale super-resolution (RSI-ASSR) methods support reconstruction at arbitrary or continuous scales, they predominantly condition on the relative scale factor and have not sufficiently investigated the absolute spatial resolution itself as a reconstruction prior, thereby disregarding the inherent spatial context of objects, which frequently leads to spatial-related distortions and compromised performance in downstream remote sensing applications. To address these challenges, we introduce SpatialSR, a SRe-centric arbitrary-scale RSISR method that leverages the spatial resolution (SRe) of remote sensing images (RSI) as an essential prior for super-resolution reconstruction. Distinct from existing SR methods, SpatialSR aims to restore high-resolution remote sensing images with a target SRe (typically set to 0.1m/pixel to align with the metadata of commonly used downstream task datasets). Specifically, we design a Spatial Resolution Estimation Module (SREM) to estimate the SRe of low-resolution (LR) images, thereby dynamically determining the required arbitrary scaling factor. Next, we employ a pretrained SRe-to-image diffusion model to extract SRe-specified texture-style codes, which are further incorporated into a carefully designed Resolution-aware Style Consistency Module (RSCM) to constrain the SRe-aware texture consistency of reconstructed images. Furthermore, to overcome the high computational expense inherent in diffusion-based SR methods, we wrap the iterative diffusion process as a Trajectory Consistency (TC) loss, which enables comparable reconstructed texture quality of the generative model in SpatialSR within a single step. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed SpatialSR achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on commonly used RSISR and downstream (image classification and segmentation tasks) datasets.

AI.tldr: SpatialSR is an arbitrary-scale remote sensing super-resolution method that uses the absolute spatial resolution as a prior, targets 0.1 m/pixel, and applies a trajectory consistency loss so that diffusion-quality texture is obtained in a single step; it reports state-of-the-art results on RSISR and downstream classification and segmentation datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing arbitrary-scale methods condition only on the relative scale factor and ignore absolute spatial resolution, which causes spatial distortions that harm downstream remote sensing applications.
AI.method: A Spatial Resolution Estimation Module estimates the resolution of the low-resolution image to set the scaling factor; a pretrained SRe-to-image diffusion model provides texture-style codes fed into a Resolution-aware Style Consistency Module; a Trajectory Consistency loss wraps the iterative diffusion process into a single step.
AI.result: SpatialSR achieves state-of-the-art performance on commonly used RSISR datasets and on downstream image classification and segmentation datasets; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Spatial resolution is a useful prior for remote sensing super-resolution, and diffusion-level texture quality can be reached in one step.

title: Just Image Transformers with Late-Stage Pixel Refinement
summary: Recent work on latent-free diffusion transformers has demonstrated the feasibility of training image generators without a latent VAE. This avoids compression artifacts from the VAE and simplifies the training pipeline. In particular, JiT showed that even a standard transformer can be trained to generate images when the model is trained to predict the final image ($x$-prediction). Even though JiT unlocks training efficiency comparable to latent models, it still suffers from reduced image quality likely arising from modeling the image as a collection of large patches. In this work, we revisit JiT and show that adding simple convolutional pixel-pathway layers in a post-training phase significantly improves generation quality. Moreover, we show that the added pixel-pathway does not need to be active in the early denoising stages, and can be activated as late as in the last $20\%$ of the denoising process. Our experiments on ImageNet@256 show improvements compared to the original JiT results, achieving an FID of $1.78$ (from $2.34$ with corrected sampling), without using additional losses.

AI.tldr: Adding convolutional pixel-pathway layers only in a post-training phase, active in the last 20% of denoising, improves Just Image Transformer (JiT) generation on ImageNet 256 to an FID of 1.78 from 2.34 with corrected sampling, without extra losses.
AI.motivation: JiT trains latent-free diffusion transformers to predict the clean image, but its quality suffers because it models images as a collection of large patches.
AI.method: Simple convolutional pixel-pathway layers are added in a post-training phase; the pathway does not need to be active in early denoising stages and can be activated as late as the last 20% of the denoising process.
AI.result: On ImageNet@256 the method improves over the original JiT results, reaching FID 1.78 from 2.34 with corrected sampling, without additional losses.
AI.conclusion: Late-stage pixel refinement is a cheap post-training fix for the quality loss caused by patch-level modeling in latent-free transformers.

title: VIGOR: Benchmarking Visual Rationale Correctness in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are typically evaluated by whether they produce correct answers, but correctness alone does not reveal whether their outputs are supported by the right visual evidence. We introduce VIGOR, a benchmark for evaluating VIsually GrOunded Rationales in MLLMs. VIGOR represents visual rationales as explicit concepts paired with pixel-level groundings, covering multiple abstraction levels including low-level visual properties, intermediate structures, objects, parts and high-level motion, relations. To construct VIGOR at scale, we develop an automatic annotation framework that reuses existing dense supervision when available and generates missing concept groundings through proposal-based annotation followed by conservative multimodal verification. Using VIGOR, we evaluate whether MLLMs "look at what they say" by comparing model-derived visual evidence for each expressed concept against annotated ground-truth rationales. Our results show that current MLLMs exhibit limited visual rationale correctness and reveal distinct grounding failures across concept levels. VIGOR provides a benchmark and scalable data construction pipeline for studying whether MLLM outputs are supported by appropriate visual evidence. Code is available at this https URL

AI.tldr: VIGOR is a benchmark that checks whether an MLLM's expressed visual concepts are supported by the right pixel-level visual evidence, not only whether answers are correct; current MLLMs show limited visual rationale correctness.
AI.motivation: Answer correctness alone does not reveal whether MLLM outputs are supported by the right visual evidence.
AI.method: Visual rationales are represented as explicit concepts paired with pixel-level groundings across abstraction levels, from low-level visual properties to intermediate structures, objects, parts and high-level motion and relations; an automatic annotation framework reuses dense supervision where available and generates missing groundings through proposal-based annotation and conservative multimodal verification.
AI.result: Current MLLMs exhibit limited visual rationale correctness and distinct grounding failures across concept levels; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: VIGOR provides a benchmark and scalable data construction pipeline for studying whether MLLM outputs are supported by appropriate visual evidence.

title: Continuous Angular Control in Text-to-Image Generation via Geometric Token Encoding
summary: Text-to-image diffusion models can render a photorealistic analog clock but cannot control the time it displays. Across four pretrained models, fewer than 1% of generated clocks place both hands within 6 degrees of the requested time; the models instead collapse onto visually dominant configurations such as the canonical 10:10 pose. The same failure appears when a specific fraction of a circular object is requested, where models return complete or conventionally sliced objects. We observe that these two failures share a geometric structure: both target quantities can be parameterized by angular variables. We introduce a geometric token encoding framework that conditions generation directly on these angles. Each angular component is encoded as a periodic sine-cosine feature and projected into a role-specific token embedding that is injected into the prompt before a frozen text encoder. To spatially ground these tokens without requiring localization input at inference, we introduce Stochastic Localization Relaxation (SLR), which stochastically relaxes attention supervision from component-level to object-level to unconstrained localization during training. For clocks, we additionally introduce a hand-swap preference objective that discourages assigning the correct angles to the wrong hand roles. On analog clocks our method reaches 63-78% Acc@6 degrees across evaluation methods, compared with below 1% for the baselines. On circular-fraction generation, it achieves 89.5% Acc@0.10, while maintaining 88.8% on unseen object categories and 84.9% on unseen target values, compared with roughly 20% for pretrained baselines.

AI.tldr: A geometric token encoding framework conditions text-to-image diffusion on angles, raising analog clock time accuracy within 6 degrees from below 1% to 63-78% and circular-fraction accuracy to 89.5%, where pretrained baselines reach roughly 20%.
AI.motivation: Pretrained text-to-image models render photorealistic clocks but cannot control the displayed time (fewer than 1% of clocks match the requested time within 6 degrees across four models), and cannot produce a requested fraction of a circular object.
AI.method: Each angular component is encoded as a periodic sine-cosine feature and projected into a role-specific token embedding injected into the prompt before a frozen text encoder; Stochastic Localization Relaxation relaxes attention supervision from component-level to object-level to unconstrained localization during training; a hand-swap preference objective is added for clocks.
AI.result: On analog clocks the method reaches 63-78% Acc@6 degrees across evaluation methods, versus below 1% for baselines; on circular-fraction generation it reaches 89.5% Acc@0.10, with 88.8% on unseen object categories and 84.9% on unseen target values, compared with roughly 20% for pretrained baselines.
AI.conclusion: Conditioning directly on geometric angle tokens gives continuous angular control in text-to-image generation that generalizes to unseen categories and target values.

title: GroundCascade: Selective Second Opinions for GUI Grounding
summary: Graphical user interface (GUI) grounding maps a screenshot and a natural-language instruction to the screen location where an agent should act. Zoomed views can reveal small targets but may lose the context needed to identify them. We introduce GroundCascade, a training-free controller that uses agreement between a grounder's full-screen and zoomed predictions to decide when to consult a complementary model. It selects between zoomed predictions while preserving corroborated full-screen locations. An optional Finalizer predicts from an unmarked joint crop when disagreement remains (Full); omitting it yields the two-stage Selective variant. GroundCascade reaches 85.33% on ScreenSpot-Pro with Indeed-UI-32B/8B/32B and 88.43% on the visible-target OSWorld-G-Refined subset with Qwen3.6-27B/3.8-27B/3.8-27B, gains of 2.66 and 2.35 percentage points over the stronger standalone two-pass grounder. On UI-Vision, GroundCascade reaches 72.20% category-balanced accuracy, with Selective slightly higher at 72.28%. Across these three evaluations, GroundCascade in Full mode uses 2.42-2.73 calls per request, 31-39% fewer than unconditionally acquiring both models' two-pass predictions. At matched second-model call budgets, selective acquisition gains 1.52-2.56 points over standalone Two-pass, compared with 0.22-0.69 points from stratified random acquisition. GroundCascade leads the official ScreenSpot-Pro leaderboard and exceeds reported GUI-specialist comparisons on OSWorld-G-Refined and UI-Vision, subject to differences in external evaluation protocols.

AI.tldr: GroundCascade is a training-free GUI grounding controller that consults a complementary model only when a grounder's full-screen and zoomed predictions disagree, reaching 85.33% on ScreenSpot-Pro with 31-39% fewer calls than unconditional two-pass acquisition.
AI.motivation: Zoomed views can reveal small GUI targets but may lose the context needed to identify them.
AI.method: Agreement between full-screen and zoomed predictions decides when to consult a second model; the controller selects between zoomed predictions while keeping corroborated full-screen locations; an optional Finalizer predicts from an unmarked joint crop when disagreement remains (Full mode), and omitting it gives the two-stage Selective variant.
AI.result: GroundCascade reaches 85.33% on ScreenSpot-Pro with Indeed-UI-32B/8B/32B and 88.43% on the visible-target OSWorld-G-Refined subset with Qwen3.6-27B/3.8-27B/3.8-27B, gains of 2.66 and 2.35 points over the stronger standalone two-pass grounder; 72.20% category-balanced accuracy on UI-Vision (Selective 72.28%); Full mode uses 2.42-2.73 calls per request, 31-39% fewer than unconditional acquisition; selective acquisition gains 1.52-2.56 points over standalone two-pass at matched budgets.
AI.conclusion: Selective second opinions improve grounding at lower cost and lead the official ScreenSpot-Pro leaderboard, subject to differences in external evaluation protocols.

title: Multimodal Judges Flag, Humans Decide: A Review-and-Edit Framework for AI-Generated Product Video Ads
comment: Accepted at the WVAQ workshop at WACV 2027
summary: Generative pipelines can now turn every product page of an e-commerce catalog into a short video ad, but deciding whether such an ad is usable is not one good-or-bad call. We describe how we operationalized the review and editing of these ads so that both can keep pace with generation: reviewers go through each ad scene by scene and answer six questions, on the product, scene quality, pronunciation, script, sound and captions; judges built from vision-language, speech and language models file each finding under the matching question, and reviewers accept or reject each finding and add what the judges missed. Each confirmed issue then opens an edit tool matched to it. The questions and the routing from a finding to its fix do not depend on the models that generate the ad. Across 120 ads from our pipeline, reviewed with judge findings on screen, reviewers marked the product wrong on 60% of scenes, and script, caption or sound problems on under 10% each. On 60 of these ads, they marked the product wrong on 58% of scenes, far more than the 26% marked by two reviewers who later saw the ads with the judges hidden; one reviewer who saw the ads both ways marked 57% with judge findings and 19% without. On 120 blind-labeled scenes, a product judge that watches the clip with the catalog photos reached AUC 0.84, while video-quality and photo-similarity scores were close to chance. We tune the judges for recall: the product judge catches nearly all defects but also flags many clean scenes, so reviewers decide; together, the judges widen what reviewers mark and reviewers add what the judges miss. Without judge findings, one reviewer's marking faded over a session. We release a review-portal template and our review data (120 ads and 562 scenes with judge findings and human marks, plus 120 blind-labeled scenes with baseline scores) at this https URL.

AI.tldr: A review-and-edit framework in which vision-language, speech and language model judges flag issues in AI-generated product video ads and humans decide; across 120 ads reviewers marked the product wrong on 60% of scenes with judge findings on screen.
AI.motivation: Whether a generated e-commerce product video ad is usable is not a single good-or-bad call, and review has to keep pace with generation.
AI.method: Reviewers go through each scene and answer six questions (product, scene quality, pronunciation, script, sound, captions); judges file each finding under the matching question; reviewers accept or reject each finding and add what the judges missed; each confirmed issue opens an edit tool matched to it. The judges are tuned for recall.
AI.result: Across 120 ads, reviewers marked the product wrong on 60% of scenes, with script, caption or sound problems under 10% each. On 60 of these ads they marked the product wrong on 58% of scenes, versus 26% for two reviewers who later saw the ads with judges hidden; one reviewer marked 57% with judge findings and 19% without. On 120 blind-labeled scenes the product judge reached AUC 0.84, while video-quality and photo-similarity scores were close to chance.
AI.conclusion: Judges widen what reviewers mark and reviewers add what judges miss, so human decisions stay central; the review portal template and the review data are released.

title: X Marks the Spot: Diffusion for Image Geolocalization with Location Representations
summary: Image geolocalization predicts the location at which a photo was taken. Accurate geolocalization requires discriminating between both physically and semantically adjacent areas on Earth. However, prior diffusion-based approaches predict locations by generating coordinates, which are semantically unstable over space. We avoid this limitation by learning geolocalization behavior in the pretrained representation spaces of location encoders, which provide both positional and semantic understanding. To make this space usable for coordinate prediction, we introduce a Location Autoencoder (LAE), which pairs a frozen location encoder with a learned decoder mapping embeddings back to coordinates with kilometer-level accuracy worldwide. In the LAE space, we train DIG, a latent diffusion model that transports noise to location embeddings conditioned on image features. DIG consistently outperforms coordinate-based generative models and sets a new state of the art for parametric geolocalization on three benchmarks: OSV-5M, Im2GPS3k, and YFCC4k. Notably, DIG is the first generative model to outperform retrieval-based methods, and further improves retrieve-and-rerank systems when used as a prior. Code and models will be released.

AI.tldr: DIG is a latent diffusion model that generates image-conditioned location embeddings in the pretrained space of a location encoder, decoded to coordinates by a Location Autoencoder; it sets a new state of the art for parametric geolocalization on OSV-5M, Im2GPS3k and YFCC4k and is the first generative model to outperform retrieval-based methods.
AI.motivation: Prior diffusion-based approaches predict locations by generating coordinates, which are semantically unstable over space.
AI.method: A Location Autoencoder pairs a frozen location encoder with a learned decoder that maps embeddings back to coordinates with kilometer-level accuracy worldwide; DIG transports noise to location embeddings conditioned on image features in this latent space; DIG also improves retrieve-and-rerank systems when used as a prior.
AI.result: DIG consistently outperforms coordinate-based generative models and sets a new state of the art for parametric geolocalization on OSV-5M, Im2GPS3k and YFCC4k; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Learning geolocalization in location-encoder representation space gives a stronger generative model than generating coordinates, and it complements retrieval-based systems.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep Learning Models for Geographic Atrophy Segmentation in En Face OCT Images
summary: Background: Geographic atrophy (GA) is an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). It causes irreversible vision loss due to progressive degeneration of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and photoreceptors. Accurate segmentation of GA in en-face image is crucial for early diagnosis, monitoring disease progression, and developing personalized treatment strategies. However, existing deep learning approaches are typically evaluated using single architectures and single-device datasets, limiting insight into relative performance and cross-device robustness. Methods: We trained and systematically compared five deep learning architectures for GA segmentation: Nested U-Net, ResU-Net, nnUnet, Swin-Unet and MedSegDiff model, together with a thresholding based classical baseline. The models were trained on a dataset of en-face OCT images derived from 269 OCT volumes from two different devices, following a three-step preprocessing technique involving normalization and inpainting to enhance the quality of the en-face images. Results: On the fixed held-out validation set comprising OCT scans from both Cirrus (R) (Carl Zeiss Meditec, Inc., USA) and Spectralis (R) (Heidelberg Engineering, Germany) devices, nnUnet achieved the highest mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.8882 +/- 0.0033. The other models yielded the following Dice scores: Nested U-Net (0.7932 +/- 0.0423), ResU-Net (0.8453 +/- 0.0074), Swin-Unet (0.6886 +/- 0.0294), and Diffusion model (0.7959 +/- 0.0242).
