Conclusions: nnUnet framework, demonstrated most reliable performance for GA segmentation in en-face OCT under limited data conditions. It offers the best balance of accuracy, stability, and efficiency for GA quantification.

AI.tldr: Five deep learning architectures and a thresholding baseline were compared for geographic atrophy segmentation in en face OCT images; nnUNet achieved the highest mean Dice of 0.8882 on a held-out set spanning Cirrus and Spectralis devices.
AI.motivation: Existing deep learning approaches for geographic atrophy segmentation are evaluated with single architectures and single-device datasets, which limits insight into relative performance and cross-device robustness.
AI.method: Nested U-Net, ResU-Net, nnUNet, Swin-Unet and MedSegDiff were trained on en face OCT images derived from 269 volumes of two devices, after normalization and inpainting preprocessing, and compared with a thresholding-based classical baseline.
AI.result: On the fixed held-out validation set from Cirrus and Spectralis scans, nnUNet reached mean DSC 0.8882 +/- 0.0033; ResU-Net 0.8453 +/- 0.0074, Nested U-Net 0.7932 +/- 0.0423, the diffusion model 0.7959 +/- 0.0242 and Swin-Unet 0.6886 +/- 0.0294.
AI.conclusion: nnUNet was the most reliable and best balanced option for GA segmentation and quantification in en face OCT under limited data conditions.

title: Multimodal Road Closure Mapping via Cross-Modal Graph Attention
comment: Published at ACM SIGSPATIAL 2026. 11 pages, 4 figures
summary: Accurate and timely identification of road closures is critical for large-scale navigation and logistics systems, yet remains challenging due to the need to jointly reason over visual evidence, spatial context, and road network topology. Existing approaches either rely on manual map updates or focus on detecting closure-related objects without resolving which road segment is affected. In this work, we introduce a unified multimodal and multitask framework that jointly performs road closure classification (no, partial, complete) and road segment association within a single learning architecture. Our model integrates graph-structured map data, satellite imagery augmented with projected street-level detections, and street-view images using modality-specific encoders and cross-modal transformer attention, enabling explicit reasoning over visual cues and network topology. Evaluated on nearly 20K real-world scenarios collected from a large-scale commercial vehicle fleet, our approach achieves 72.7% closure classification accuracy and 60% road segment association accuracy, outperforming frontier vision-language models by over 28 percentage points on closure classification while being over 4,000x smaller and 100x faster at inference. Extensive ablations demonstrate the importance of cross-modal attention, edge-aware pooling, and graph message passing for accurate geospatial reasoning. This work establishes the first benchmark for joint road closure classification and segment-level attribution, and shows that task-specific architectural inductive biases substantially outperform general-purpose multimodal models for structured geospatial understanding.

AI.tldr: A multimodal, multitask graph-attention framework jointly classifies road closures (no, partial, complete) and associates them with road segments, reaching 72.7% closure classification accuracy and 60% segment association accuracy on nearly 20K real-world scenarios.
AI.motivation: Road closures are critical for navigation and logistics, but identification relies on manual map updates or detects closure-related objects without resolving which road segment is affected.
AI.method: Modality-specific encoders handle graph-structured map data, satellite imagery with projected street-level detections, and street-view images; cross-modal transformer attention and graph message passing, with edge-aware pooling, combine them in one architecture.
AI.result: On nearly 20K real-world scenarios from a large commercial vehicle fleet, the approach reaches 72.7% closure classification accuracy and 60% road segment association accuracy, outperforming frontier vision-language models by over 28 percentage points on classification while being over 4,000x smaller and 100x faster at inference.
AI.conclusion: Task-specific architectural inductive biases can substantially outperform general-purpose multimodal models on structured geospatial understanding, and the work establishes the first benchmark for joint closure classification and segment-level attribution.

title: Image Quality and the Reliability of Fabric-Density Measurement: Counting Threads from Smartphone Photos Through a Pick Glass
comment: Accepted at the WVAQ workshop at WACV 2027
summary: Thread density, the threads per inch along and across a woven fabric, is a basic specification that buyers check whenever fabric is sold. Without laboratory instruments, inspectors count it slowly, by eye, through a pick glass, a folding 10$\times$ magnifier with a one-inch window. A smartphone photo through that glass could make the check faster and leave a record. We judge such a photo by what it is used for, as in task-based image quality: it is good if the thread count from it is within $\pm$5% of the true count, a common tolerance in fabric specifications. We introduce PickGlass-TPI: 76 factory scenes of 44 fabric patches, each counted in an open annotation tool by a textile-trained annotator, whose counts are the reference. On it we benchmark frontier and open vision-language models, CNNs, counting specialists and a training-free spectral counter (PG-Lattice). No method agrees with the reference within the tolerance. The best methods are off by about a quarter: a small open model that we tuned only on synthetic images (Molmo2-4B, 25%) is level with the best frontier model, GPT-6.1-sol (27% when asked directly, 25% given four magnified close-ups of the window). Both err less than a non-expert annotator (37%), but only the tuned model also beats, on both error measures, a baseline that guesses each scene's density as the average of the others. PG-Lattice most often repeats its count within 5% across two photos of the same patch, but its misses, like GPT-6.1-sol's errors, are often a factor of two. Even the reference repeats a count across such re-shoots only to a median 9%, so one photo cannot yet be shown to meet $\pm$5%; the image quality that matters is reliability across re-shoots. Generic no-reference quality scores chosen before labeling do not rank PG-Lattice's error, and generative enhancement raises perceptual scores but does not reliably improve the count.

AI.tldr: PickGlass-TPI is a benchmark of 76 factory scenes of 44 fabric patches for counting threads per inch from smartphone photos taken through a pick glass; no method agrees with the reference within the plus or minus 5% tolerance, and the best methods are off by about a quarter.
AI.motivation: Manual thread counting is slow, and a smartphone photo through a pick glass could make the check faster and leave a record, but the photo's usefulness is unproven.
AI.method: Image quality is judged by task, as whether the thread count from the photo is within plus or minus 5% of the true count; a textile-trained annotator provides reference counts; frontier and open VLMs, CNNs, counting specialists and a training-free spectral counter (PG-Lattice) are benchmarked.
AI.result: The best methods are off by about a quarter: Molmo2-4B, tuned only on synthetic images, is at 25% and level with GPT-6.1-sol at 27% when asked directly and 25% given four magnified close-ups; a non-expert annotator is off 37%; only the tuned model also beats a per-scene average-density baseline on both error measures. PG-Lattice most often repeats its count within 5% across two photos of the same patch, but its misses are often a factor of two.
AI.conclusion: One photo cannot yet be shown to meet the plus or minus 5% tolerance, since even the reference repeats counts across re-shoots only to a median 9%; reliability across re-shoots is the image quality that matters, and generic quality scores and generative enhancement do not capture it.

title: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood
comment: Accepted as NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight paper. Project page at \hyperlink{this https URL}{this URL}
summary: Children's earliest years are a period of intense social learning, during which meaning is built through gaze, gesture, and physical contact. Yet, this critical aspect of social interaction remains under-evaluated in multimodal video understanding, as existing benchmarks prioritize the conversation-driven interactions of adults. We address this gap with \bench ($\textbf{N}$aturalistic $\textbf{E}$arly-childhood $\textbf{S}$ocial in$\textbf{T}$eractions), the first child-centric benchmark for nonverbal social reasoning. \bench comprises \totalvids manually annotated clips ($\sim$12s) curated for diversity across naturalistic settings, cultural contexts, and developmental stages. Beyond a lack of data, targeted model improvement in this domain is hindered by coarse evaluation schemas that conflate basic perception with higher-order reasoning. To resolve this, \bench introduces a compositional schema that builds atomic interaction cues into progressive levels of social reasoning: contextual, behavioral, interpersonal, and open-ended descriptions. Extensive analysis of state-of-the-art Vision-Language Models (VLMs) reveals a stark performance collapse: despite strong contextual recognition, models exhibit substantial gaps in decoding precise behavioral and interpersonal cues. We trace these failures to specific biases, including poor consequence grounding and temporal sensitivity. Finally, we ground \bench in real-world applications by evaluating VLMs using domain adaptation strategies. Ultimately, \bench provides a rigorous testbed for advancing socially grounded artificial intelligence in early childhood. Project page: this https URL.

AI.tldr: A child-centric benchmark of about 12-second annotated clips tests nonverbal social reasoning in early childhood, and state-of-the-art VLMs show strong contextual recognition but a sharp performance collapse on behavioral and interpersonal cues.
AI.motivation: Existing video benchmarks prioritize adult conversational interaction, leaving early-childhood nonverbal social interaction under-evaluated, and coarse evaluation schemas conflate basic perception with higher-order reasoning.
AI.method: A compositional schema builds atomic interaction cues into four progressive levels of social reasoning: contextual, behavioral, interpersonal and open-ended descriptions; clips are curated for diversity across naturalistic settings, cultural contexts and developmental stages.
AI.result: VLMs show substantial gaps in decoding precise behavioral and interpersonal cues despite strong contextual recognition; the failures are traced to poor consequence grounding and temporal sensitivity; domain adaptation strategies are also evaluated. The abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark provides a rigorous testbed for socially grounded AI in early childhood and exposes failure modes that current VLMs miss.

title: Rethinking Evaluation for Video Capsule Endoscopy: Validation Protocol, Source-Video Diversity, and Cross-Dataset Shift
summary: Automated video capsule endoscopy (VCE) classification remains challenging due to severe class imbalance, limited source-video diversity, and variations in image appearance across datasets. Although deep learning models have demonstrated promising performance on established benchmarks, their reliability under different validation protocols and external dataset shift remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we introduce DMSNet, a deformable adaptive multi-scale edge-guided attention network integrating adaptive multi-scale feature fusion, deformable lesion refinement, edge-guided attention, and sparse feature selection. We benchmark DMSNet against 18 representative convolutional, transformer-based, and pretrained vision architectures on Kvasir-Capsule under random frame-level and source-video-disjoint validation protocols. We further identify source-video overlap between the original training and test splits and evaluate model performance on both the complete test set and a source-video-disjoint subset. Under random frame-level validation, DMSNet achieves an MCC of 0.442 $\pm$ 0.020 on complete test set and 0.456 $\pm$ 0.037 on the source-video-disjoint subset. On the external CV2024 dataset, ConvNeXt-Tiny achieves the highest MCC of 0.207, while performance degrades substantially across architectures relative to in-domain evaluation. We further investigate source-video diversity using a per-class cap of 200 training frames. With the total training-set size held fixed, increasing the maximum source-video coverage from four to eight improves MCC for 17 of 19 evaluated architectures. Overall, these findings demonstrate that model rankings and classification performance depend substantially on evaluation protocol, training-source diversity, and cross-dataset shift, emphasizing the need for source-aware validation and rigorous external evaluation of VCE classification systems.

AI.tldr: Benchmarks DMSNet against 18 convolutional, transformer and pretrained architectures for video capsule endoscopy classification on Kvasir-Capsule and shows that model rankings and performance depend strongly on the validation protocol, source-video diversity and cross-dataset shift.
AI.motivation: Video capsule endoscopy classification suffers from severe class imbalance, limited source-video diversity and appearance variation across datasets, and the reliability of deep models under different validation protocols and external dataset shift is insufficiently understood; the original training and test splits also share source videos.
AI.method: DMSNet is a deformable adaptive multi-scale edge-guided attention network with adaptive multi-scale feature fusion, deformable lesion refinement, edge-guided attention and sparse feature selection; it is evaluated under random frame-level and source-video-disjoint validation, on the external CV2024 dataset, and with a per-class cap of 200 training frames that varies source-video coverage from four to eight.
AI.result: Under random frame-level validation DMSNet reaches MCC 0.442 +/- 0.020 on the complete test set and 0.456 +/- 0.037 on the source-video-disjoint subset; on CV2024 ConvNeXt-Tiny achieves the highest MCC of 0.207 and performance degrades substantially across architectures; increasing source-video coverage from four to eight improves MCC for 17 of 19 evaluated architectures.
AI.conclusion: Model rankings and classification performance depend substantially on evaluation protocol, training-source diversity and dataset shift, so VCE classification systems need source-aware validation and rigorous external evaluation.

title: Adaptive Residual Quantization for Memory-Efficient Temporal Action Segmentation
summary: Temporal action segmentation (TAS) is commonly trained on large banks of pre-extracted frame features, but storing and replaying those features becomes a practical bottleneck for long-form video, especially in incremental TAS where past-task data must remain available to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. Recent TAS replay and condensation methods reduce this burden, but they rely on dense frame-wise annotations and allocate storage through fixed segment-level structures, limiting their flexibility for long procedural videos whose frame complexity varies substantially over time. We introduce Adaptive Residual-Quantized Variational AutoEncoder (ARQ-VAE), a compact and label-free memory representation for TAS features that learns a discrete residual quantization of frame-level video features and then adaptively truncates the residual chain on a per-frame basis, retaining only the residual prefix that best reconstructs each frame feature. This yields a practical compact feature memory that does not depend on frame-wise labels and can therefore support multiple TAS settings with the same stored representation, while a lightweight fine-tuning stage further improves reconstruction quality for the truncated codes that are actually retained. Across standard TAS benchmarks, ARQ-VAE achieves a substantially improved storage-performance trade-off over prior replay and condensation baselines. On Breakfast, our final representation reduces training-set storage from 28 GB for the original I3D feature bank to 10 MB while retaining strong downstream segmentation performance; with ASFormer, it achieves 71.5 Edit and 51.2 F1@50 in the supervised setting. We further show that the same label-free memory remains effective for incremental and unsupervised TAS. We position ARQ-VAE as a practical memory representation for TAS and a promising direction for broader dataset condensation applications.

AI.tldr: Proposes ARQ-VAE, a compact, label-free memory for temporal action segmentation features built on adaptive residual quantization, which reduces Breakfast training-set feature storage from 28 GB to 10 MB while retaining strong segmentation performance.
AI.motivation: Storing and replaying pre-extracted frame features is a bottleneck for long-form video in incremental TAS, and existing replay and condensation methods depend on dense frame-wise annotations and fixed segment-level structures that do not fit videos whose frame complexity varies over time.
AI.method: ARQ-VAE learns a discrete residual quantization of frame-level video features and adaptively truncates the residual chain per frame, keeping only the residual prefix that best reconstructs each frame feature; a lightweight fine-tuning stage improves reconstruction quality for the truncated codes that are retained.
AI.result: On Breakfast, storage falls from 28 GB for the original I3D feature bank to 10 MB; with ASFormer it achieves 71.5 Edit and 51.2 F1@50 in the supervised setting, and the same label-free memory remains effective for incremental and unsupervised TAS, with a better storage-performance trade-off than prior replay and condensation baselines across standard benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: ARQ-VAE is a practical compact memory for TAS that does not need frame-wise labels and is a promising direction for broader dataset condensation.

title: RetinexGS: Retinex-Inspired Gaussian Splatting for Low-Light RAW Reconstruction
summary: Standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) pipelines struggle with severely underexposed images, producing unstable colors, floating artifacts, and incomplete reconstructions in dark regions. To better account for noise in these low-light observations, RAW images offer a natural basis for noise-aware reconstruction by preserving linear sensor measurements and providing access to noise metadata. We present RetinexGS, a RAW-domain 3DGS framework that combines Retinex-inspired appearance modeling with sensor-informed optimization for low-light novel-view synthesis. We factorize each Gaussian's color into a view-independent base color and a shared, position- and view-dependent modulation field, regularizing the two components separately to constrain appearance learning from noisy observations. We use DNG noise metadata to weight the reconstruction loss for signal-dependent noise, while distortion-aware rendering avoids spatially resampling RAW targets. To address sparse geometry in dark regions, we introduce depth-guided initialization. We evaluate RetinexGS on three public RawNeRF scenes and two custom-captured low-light RAW scenes. With all methods trained on the same RAW inputs for each scene, RetinexGS outperforms LE3D and RawNeRF in mean sRGB PSNR by 2.18 dB and 2.71 dB respectively, across the five scenes, while supporting real-time novel-view rendering.

AI.tldr: Introduces RetinexGS, a RAW-domain 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for low-light novel-view synthesis that outperforms LE3D and RawNeRF in mean sRGB PSNR while supporting real-time rendering.
AI.motivation: Standard 3DGS pipelines produce unstable colors, floating artifacts and incomplete reconstructions on severely underexposed images, and noisy low-light observations call for noise-aware reconstruction, which RAW images support by preserving linear sensor measurements and noise metadata.
AI.method: Each Gaussian's color is factorized into a view-independent base color and a shared, position- and view-dependent modulation field, with the two components regularized separately; the reconstruction loss is weighted by DNG noise metadata for signal-dependent noise, distortion-aware rendering avoids spatially resampling RAW targets, and depth-guided initialization addresses sparse geometry in dark regions.
AI.result: On three public RawNeRF scenes and two custom low-light RAW scenes, all trained on the same RAW inputs, RetinexGS outperforms LE3D by 2.18 dB and RawNeRF by 2.71 dB in mean sRGB PSNR across the five scenes, while supporting real-time novel-view rendering.
AI.conclusion: Combining Retinex-inspired appearance modeling with sensor-informed optimization enables more accurate low-light novel-view synthesis from RAW inputs.

title: Domain adaptation of a video Foundation model for Heart Failure Diagnosis from Echocardiography
comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, accepted and presented at Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC 2026)
summary: The rapid advancement of foundation models has transformed computer vision, yet their adaptation to medical imaging, particularly purpose built foundation models for spatio temporal echocardiography videos, remains limited. In this work, we explore the feasibility of fine tuning a pretrained foundation model for video (TimeSformer) for automated diagnosis of reduced ejection fraction heart failure (HFrEF) from apical four chamber videos. The model is finetuned on the publicly available RVENet A4C dataset with a phase aware clip generation strategy that captures complementary systolic and diastolic dynamics. We employ divided space time attention, layer wise learning rate decay, and multi clip inference to enhance robustness under limited data. Experimental results show that full fine tuning of the proposed model outperforms classifier only tuning and a 3D CNN baseline. These findings highlight the potential of leveraging foundation video models for echocardiography based heart failure diagnosis and motivates further domain adaptation studies in medical imaging.

AI.tldr: Fine-tunes the pretrained video foundation model TimeSformer for diagnosing reduced ejection fraction heart failure from apical four-chamber echocardiography videos, and finds that full fine-tuning outperforms classifier-only tuning and a 3D CNN baseline.
AI.motivation: Foundation models have transformed computer vision, but their adaptation to medical imaging, particularly purpose-built foundation models for spatio-temporal echocardiography videos, remains limited.
AI.method: TimeSformer is fine-tuned on the public RVENet A4C dataset with a phase-aware clip generation strategy that captures complementary systolic and diastolic dynamics, using divided space-time attention, layer-wise learning rate decay and multi-clip inference to improve robustness under limited data.
AI.result: Full fine-tuning of the proposed model outperforms classifier-only tuning and a 3D CNN baseline for HFrEF diagnosis; the abstract reports no numerical metrics.
AI.conclusion: Leveraging foundation video models shows potential for echocardiography-based heart failure diagnosis and motivates further domain adaptation studies in medical imaging.

title: DUO: Dual Readouts of Diffusion Models for OOD Detection
summary: Diffusion models are powerful generative methods for learning and sampling from complex data distributions. Safely deploying these models requires detecting inputs that fall outside their training distribution. Because diffusion models recover clean samples from noisy inputs, reconstruction error is often used for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. This approach assumes that in-distribution (ID) inputs are reconstructed more accurately than OOD inputs. However, OOD inputs may be reconstructed equally well or even better, making this score unreliable. We therefore propose the leading sensitivity spectrum of intermediate denoising features as a complementary OOD signal and demonstrate that it remains informative when reconstruction error is misleading. We introduce DUal-readout of diffusion models for OOD detection (DUO), a fully unsupervised, training-free OOD detector that combines reconstruction error and feature sensitivity. DUO improves average AUROC by approximately 6% points over the strongest baselines while substantially reducing inference cost, and achieves SOTA on near-OOD and high-resolution benchmarks.

AI.tldr: Proposes DUO, a fully unsupervised, training-free OOD detector for diffusion models that combines reconstruction error with the leading sensitivity spectrum of intermediate denoising features, improving average AUROC by approximately 6 points over the strongest baselines.
AI.motivation: Reconstruction error is a common OOD score for diffusion models, but it assumes in-distribution inputs are reconstructed more accurately than OOD inputs, and OOD inputs may be reconstructed equally well or better, which makes the score unreliable.
AI.method: The leading sensitivity spectrum of intermediate denoising features is proposed as a complementary OOD signal, and DUO combines it with reconstruction error in a training-free detector that substantially reduces inference cost.
AI.result: DUO improves average AUROC by approximately 6 percentage points over the strongest baselines and achieves SOTA on near-OOD and high-resolution benchmarks, while substantially reducing inference cost.
AI.conclusion: Feature sensitivity remains informative when reconstruction error is misleading, so it is a useful complement for safely deploying diffusion models.

title: Domain-Adversarial Adaptation from MURA to In-House Radiographs for Improved Adult Elbow Fracture Classification
comment: 4 pages, 3 figures, Accepted and presented on SPIE Medical Imaging 2026
summary: We studied domain shift in adult elbow fracture classification from radiographs when training on a large public dataset and deploying on a small, institution-specific dataset (UofL). We implemented a domain-adversarial neural network (DANN) to align feature distributions across source (MURA) and target (UofL) domains while optimizing fracture classification. A pretrained convolutional backbone was adapted to grayscale inputs; the task head predicts fracture presence, and a gradient-reversal-based domain head encourages domain-invariant features via adversarial learning. We compared four settings: (1) Source-only, (2) Target-only (limited labels), (3) Naive merge (pooled training), and (4) DANN (MURA to UofL). Evaluation on UofL test data uses AUC-ROC, and accuracy. DANN outperformed Source-only and Naive merge baselines by reducing domain bias without overfitting to the small target set. Ablations showed that progressive adversarial weight, dataset-size-aware domain loss, and domain-balanced sampling improved stability and target performance. Results demonstrated that domain alignment is a practical path to robust clinical generalization from public to local data.

AI.tldr: Applies a domain-adversarial neural network (DANN) to align the public MURA radiograph dataset with an institution-specific UofL dataset for adult elbow fracture classification, outperforming source-only and naive-merge baselines on UofL test data.
AI.motivation: A model trained on a large public dataset may not transfer to a small institution-specific deployment dataset, and the target set has only limited labels, so domain bias must be reduced without overfitting the small target set.
AI.method: A pretrained convolutional backbone adapted to grayscale inputs feeds a fracture-presence task head and a gradient-reversal domain head that encourages domain-invariant features; four settings are compared (source-only, target-only with limited labels, naive merge and DANN), with ablations on progressive adversarial weight, dataset-size-aware domain loss and domain-balanced sampling.
AI.result: DANN outperforms source-only and naive-merge baselines on UofL test data, measured by AUC-ROC and accuracy, and the ablations show that the design choices improve stability and target performance; the abstract gives no numerical values.
AI.conclusion: Domain alignment is a practical path to robust clinical generalization from public to local data.

title: ABRR: Transforming Temporal Sentence Grounding with Wasserstein-Adaptive Refinement and Precision Ranking
comment: Accepted by IEEE Transactions on Multimedia
summary: Temporal Sentence Grounding (TSG) aims to localize temporal segments in untrimmed videos that correspond to natural language queries, a critical task for video understanding with applications in video retrieval, summarization, and human-computer interaction. Despite significant progress driven by transformer-based models, existing TSG methods suffer from two key limitations: quantization errors due to temporal downsampling, which misalign segment boundaries, and suboptimal ranking of predictions based on semantic matching rather than localization precision. To address these challenges, we propose the Adaptive Boundary Refinement and Ranking (ABRR) framework, a novel, model-agnostic post-processing approach that enhances the performance of any TSG model without retraining. ABRR integrates three innovative components: (1) Temporal Distribution Smoothing, which mitigates noise in predicted score distributions using Gaussian kernel convolution; (2) Boundary Refinement via Optimal Transport, which leverages the 2-Wasserstein distance and Sinkhorn iterations to align coarse segment boundaries with true temporal moments, grounded in Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport theory; and (3) Quality-Driven Re-Ranking, which reorders predictions using a composite score balancing localization precision and semantic relevance. By correcting quantization errors and prioritizing accurately localized segments, ABRR achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art TSG models. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including Charades-STA, ActivityNet Captions, and QVHighlights, demonstrate consistent gains at stringent IoU thresholds (e.g., IoU=0.7), alongside enhanced ranking performance. The framework's computational efficiency and compatibility with existing models make it a versatile and impactful solution for real-world TSG applications.

AI.tldr: Proposes ABRR, a model-agnostic post-processing framework that refines segment boundaries and re-ranks predictions of any temporal sentence grounding model without retraining, with consistent gains at strict IoU thresholds on Charades-STA, ActivityNet Captions and QVHighlights.
AI.motivation: Existing TSG methods suffer from quantization errors caused by temporal downsampling, which misalign segment boundaries, and they rank predictions by semantic matching rather than localization precision.
AI.method: ABRR has three components: Temporal Distribution Smoothing, which uses Gaussian kernel convolution to reduce noise in predicted score distributions; Boundary Refinement via Optimal Transport, which uses the 2-Wasserstein distance and Sinkhorn iterations to align coarse boundaries with true moments; and Quality-Driven Re-Ranking, which orders predictions by a composite score balancing localization precision and semantic relevance.
AI.result: ABRR achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art TSG models, with consistent gains at stringent IoU thresholds such as IoU=0.7 and enhanced ranking performance on Charades-STA, ActivityNet Captions and QVHighlights.
AI.conclusion: By correcting quantization errors and prioritizing accurately localized segments, ABRR is a computationally efficient and compatible refinement for existing TSG models.

title: Uni-Loc: Weakly Supervised 3D CT Pathology Localization via Spatially Grounded Vision-Language Classification
summary: Accurate localization of abnormalities in three-dimensional (3D) CT scans is essential for linking automated predictions with clinically relevant pathological findings. We propose Uni-Loc, a vision-language framework that unifies pathology classification and 3D localization using scan-level supervision. Uni-Loc derives both predictions and localization maps from spatial similarities between pathology-conditioned queries and image features. A token-to-voxel upsampling module enables high-resolution localization, while gradient-guided thresholding identifies pathology regions without additional learned parameters. Evaluated on five localization tasks comprising 355 annotated CT scans, Uni-Loc achieves macro-averaged voxel-level AUROC/AUPR of 96.1\%/34.5\%, outperforming relevance propagation (80.7%/13.9%) and gradient saliency (88.7%/8.1%). Uni-Loc also achieves classification AUROC of 88.39% on CT-RATE and 78.03% on RAD-ChestCT, improving over a matched baseline. These results demonstrate effective 3D pathology localization without requiring pathology-specific voxel-level supervision.

AI.tldr: Introduces Uni-Loc, a vision-language framework that jointly classifies and localizes pathologies in 3D CT scans using only scan-level supervision, reaching macro-averaged voxel-level AUROC/AUPR of 96.1%/34.5% across five localization tasks.
AI.motivation: Linking automated 3D CT predictions to clinically relevant pathological findings requires localization, but voxel-level supervision is costly, and existing relevance propagation and gradient saliency localizers are less accurate.
AI.method: Pathology-conditioned queries are compared with image features by spatial similarity to produce both predictions and localization maps; a token-to-voxel upsampling module enables high-resolution localization, and gradient-guided thresholding identifies pathology regions without additional learned parameters.
AI.result: On 355 annotated CT scans across five localization tasks, Uni-Loc achieves macro-averaged voxel-level AUROC/AUPR of 96.1%/34.5%, versus 80.7%/13.9% for relevance propagation and 88.7%/8.1% for gradient saliency; classification AUROC is 88.39% on CT-RATE and 78.03% on RAD-ChestCT, improving over a matched baseline.
AI.conclusion: Effective 3D pathology localization is achievable without pathology-specific voxel-level supervision.

title: How Hyperbolic Are Hyperbolic Vision-Language Models?
summary: Hyperbolic vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as a rapidly growing area of research, reporting strong zero-shot performance alongside an interpretable embedding space in which radius orders representations by generality. But how hyperbolic are hyperbolic VLMs in practice? We investigate this at the exponential map, the single operation through which curvature enters an otherwise Euclidean network. We show that across MERU, HyCoCLIP, ARGENT, and PHyCLIP, the exponential map is well approximated by the identity function, i.e., pairwise distances and angles in the pre-map Euclidean space barely change under projection, and removing the map at inference leaves evaluation scores unchanged. Motivated by this observation, we train Euclidean VLMs on CC3M from scratch under the same hierarchy losses. Over roughly the final 90% of the training steps, the training statistics are nearly indistinguishable from those of their hyperbolic counterparts, and the resulting models match the evaluation scores and recover the same radial distributions. Our findings establish Euclidean space as a sufficient substrate for hierarchical vision-language learning as it is currently practiced, and motivate new paradigms in which hyperbolic geometry can deliver on its theoretical promise. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: Shows that in hyperbolic vision-language models the exponential map is nearly the identity, and that Euclidean VLMs trained from scratch match their hyperbolic counterparts on evaluation scores and radial distributions, suggesting Euclidean space suffices for current hierarchical VLM learning.
AI.motivation: Hyperbolic VLMs report strong zero-shot performance and an interpretable radius-generality ordering, but it is unclear how hyperbolic they are in practice, since curvature enters only through the exponential map.
AI.method: The exponential map is examined in MERU, HyCoCLIP, ARGENT and PHyCLIP by comparing pairwise distances and angles before and after projection and by removing the map at inference; Euclidean VLMs are then trained on CC3M from scratch under the same hierarchy losses and compared on training statistics and evaluation scores.
AI.result: The exponential map is well approximated by the identity, so pairwise distances and angles barely change under projection and removing it leaves evaluation scores unchanged; over roughly the final 90% of training steps the Euclidean models' statistics are nearly indistinguishable from the hyperbolic ones, and they match evaluation scores and recover the same radial distributions.
AI.conclusion: Euclidean space is a sufficient substrate for hierarchical vision-language learning as it is currently practiced, which motivates new paradigms in which hyperbolic geometry can deliver its theoretical promise.

title: Prompt2Echo (P2Echo): Text-Prompted Multi-View Echocardiography Segmentation with One Model
summary: Automated segmentation in multi-view echocardiography is essential for comprehensive cardiac assessment, yet remains challenging due to substantial anatomical and appearance variability across standard acoustic windows. In this paper, we present P2Echo, a unified framework capable of segmenting diverse cardiac structures across multiple standard echocardiographic views using a single model controlled by structured view-aware text prompts. Unlike recent foundation model adaptations that rely on implicit latent priors, P2Echo explicitly conditions the segmentation process via a novel Dynamic Image-Text Alignment (DyITA) module. DyITA integrates a differentiable routing mechanism and token differential operators to dynamically modulate decoder features according to the requested view and target structure. This allows the network to adaptively switch its processing pathways for different views without architectural changes. Extensive experiments on a large-scale internal dataset (seen during training) and held-out evaluation on three external datasets demonstrate that P2Echo matches or exceeds both view-specific specialists and state-of-the-art universal models at a fraction of their computational cost, offering an efficient, controllable solution for multi-plane cardiac analysis. Code is available at: this https URL.

AI.tldr: Presents P2Echo, a single model that segments diverse cardiac structures across standard echocardiographic views, controlled by structured view-aware text prompts through a Dynamic Image-Text Alignment module, matching or exceeding view-specific specialists and universal models at a fraction of their computational cost.
AI.motivation: Multi-view echocardiography segmentation is difficult because of anatomical and appearance variability across acoustic windows, and recent foundation model adaptations rely on implicit latent priors rather than explicit conditioning on the requested view and structure.
AI.method: The DyITA module integrates a differentiable routing mechanism and token differential operators to dynamically modulate decoder features according to the requested view and target structure, letting the network switch processing pathways without architectural changes.
AI.result: On a large-scale internal dataset seen during training and on held-out evaluation over three external datasets, P2Echo matches or exceeds both view-specific specialists and state-of-the-art universal models at a fraction of their computational cost.
AI.conclusion: P2Echo offers an efficient and controllable solution for multi-plane cardiac analysis.

title: Camera3R: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Heterogeneous Camera Models
comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
summary: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction (3R) from unconstrained multi-view images has recently emerged as a prominent research direction in 3D computer vision. Various foundational reconstruction models have been proposed with different architectures and reconstruction paradigms. Despite being trained on large-scale perspective datasets with substantial computational resources, these models generally struggle to generalize to non-perspective images. This limitation hinders their deployment in applications involving arbitrary, unknown, and potentially heterogeneous camera models. To build on the capabilities of existing reconstruction models with minimal retraining, we propose Camera3R, a low-rank adaptation framework that efficiently extends perspective-pretrained 3R networks to any other camera models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, with only 0.5% additional parameters and less than a day of training, Camera3R adapts a foundational 3D reconstruction model to non-perspective cameras while fully preserving its original performance on perspective inputs. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: Proposes Camera3R, a low-rank adaptation framework that extends perspective-pretrained feed-forward 3D reconstruction networks to non-perspective and heterogeneous camera models with about 0.5% additional parameters, while fully preserving performance on perspective inputs.
AI.motivation: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models trained on large perspective datasets generalize poorly to non-perspective images, which limits their deployment with arbitrary, unknown and potentially heterogeneous camera models.
AI.method: A low-rank adaptation framework extends existing perspective-pretrained 3R networks to other camera models with minimal retraining, adding a small set of trainable low-rank parameters.
AI.result: With only 0.5% additional parameters and less than a day of training, Camera3R adapts a foundational 3D reconstruction model to non-perspective cameras while fully preserving its original performance on perspective inputs.
AI.conclusion: Existing reconstruction models can be extended cheaply to diverse camera models, broadening their applicability to arbitrary camera setups.

title: Hand-Object Contact Transition Detection in Egocentric Video
summary: This paper tackles the task of hand-object contact transition detection in egocentric video, which aims to localize the two temporal boundaries of a contact episode: the moment a hand first establishes contact with an object (touch) and the moment contact is released (release). We propose a unified framework that jointly models the interacting hand and object to accurately localize both transition types. The proposed framework augments hand-centric spatiotemporal representations with object-aware features learned directly from the video and introduces a transition-aware event spotting formulation tailored to contact transitions, without relying on external object or hand-object interaction detectors during inference. To support this task, we present ContactTransition, a dataset comprising 4,021 egocentric videos with 8,498 touch and 8,077 release annotations, together with object-of-interest supervision. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms strong two-stage and end-to-end event-spotting baselines on both transition types. Finally, we show that detected contact transitions provide effective temporal anchors for downstream egocentric hand-object reasoning.

AI.tldr: Presents a unified framework and the ContactTransition dataset (4,021 egocentric videos with 8,498 touch and 8,077 release annotations) for detecting when hand-object contact begins and ends, outperforming two-stage and end-to-end event-spotting baselines without external detectors at inference.
AI.motivation: Egocentric video contact episodes need both their touch and release boundaries localized, yet the task lacks a dataset and a formulation tailored to contact transitions, and methods relying on external object or hand-object interaction detectors add dependencies at inference.
AI.method: The framework jointly models the interacting hand and object, augmenting hand-centric spatiotemporal representations with object-aware features learned directly from the video and using a transition-aware event spotting formulation for contact transitions; the dataset provides object-of-interest supervision.
AI.result: The method consistently outperforms strong two-stage and end-to-end event-spotting baselines on both touch and release transitions, and the detected contact transitions provide effective temporal anchors for downstream egocentric hand-object reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Contact transition detection is a useful temporal primitive for egocentric hand-object understanding.

title: When Reconstruction Helps Event-Camera Person Triggers
comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, ancillary score tables and recomputation script
summary: Event cameras record asynchronous changes in brightness. To use a general visual model as a recording trigger, a system must represent these measurements in a form the model can interpret. We compare direct grayscale accumulation, two temporal encodings, and two intensity reconstructors on paired real event data. On 192 windows from four held-out DSEC recordings, thresholds calibrated only on development data yielded 40 of 52 person detections and 12 of 140 background positives with E2VID. The strongest direct temporal encoding at an admissible fixed cutoff yielded 14 detections and seven background positives. A retrospective comparison at a common 10% background-positive cap yielded 40 detections for E2VID and at most 19 for any direct encoding. FireNet+ had lower preparation cost and produced 21 detections with zero observed background positives at its frozen cutoff. On the same 192 windows, Qwen3-VL-4B yielded 33/52, 2/140 with E2VID and 9/52, 9/140 with the highest-recall direct rendering, the three-bin image (person detections, background positives). A 96-second exploratory replay illustrates the sensitivity of episode capture and recording starts to cutoff selection. The experiments identify a detection benefit from reconstruction under controlled input history and distinguish it from the cost and false starts of continuous triggering.

AI.tldr: Compares ways of turning event-camera streams into inputs for a person-recording trigger and finds that E2VID intensity reconstruction gives more person detections at a low background false-positive rate than direct temporal encodings, at a higher preparation cost than FireNet+.
AI.motivation: A general visual model used as a recording trigger on event-camera data needs the asynchronous brightness changes represented in a form it can interpret, and continuous triggering risks costly false starts.
AI.method: Direct grayscale accumulation, two temporal encodings and two intensity reconstructors (E2VID and FireNet+) are compared on paired real event data from 192 windows across four held-out DSEC recordings, with thresholds calibrated only on development data; Qwen3-VL-4B is evaluated on the same windows, including a three-bin image rendering.
AI.result: With E2VID at calibrated thresholds, 40 of 52 person detections and 12 of 140 background positives; the strongest direct temporal encoding at an admissible fixed cutoff gives 14 detections and seven background positives; at a common 10% background-positive cap E2VID yields 40 detections versus at most 19 for any direct encoding; FireNet+ gives 21 detections with zero observed background positives at its frozen cutoff; Qwen3-VL-4B gives 33/52 with 2/140 background positives on E2VID and 9/52 with 9/140 on the highest-recall direct rendering.
AI.conclusion: Reconstruction gives a detection benefit under controlled input history that is distinct from the cost and false starts of continuous triggering, and cutoff selection strongly affects episode capture and recording starts in the exploratory 96-second replay.

title: Reasoning-Aware Relational Representation Learning for Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation
comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026, codes are available at project page this https URL
summary: Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation (OV-SGG) requires models to recognize visual relationships beyond the training vocabulary, yet existing methods often rely on dataset-specific object--predicate co-occurrence patterns. Under long-tailed distributions and noisy object localization, such reliance leads to biased, entangled relation representations, limiting both rare-relation recognition and generalization to unseen predicates. To address these challenges, we propose RaRe, a reasoning-aware relational representation learning framework that transforms MLLM-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) rationales into structured relation embeddings. Rather than using CoT only as an intermediate reasoning trace for final prediction, RaRe directly optimizes the rationale-derived representation space to improve inter-relation discriminability. Specifically, RaRe first aligns rationale embeddings with textualized relation descriptions through self-supervised contrastive learning, and then refines rationale generation with a specificity-oriented reinforcement learning objective that encourages semantically object-pair-specific relational evidence. Experiments on VG150 and PSG demonstrate improved category-balanced recognition over existing baselines, while the additional gains from learning vary across datasets and proposal settings. Code available at: this https URL.

AI.tldr: Proposes RaRe, which turns MLLM chain-of-thought rationales into structured relation embeddings through contrastive alignment and a specificity-oriented reinforcement learning objective, improving category-balanced recognition for open-vocabulary scene graph generation on VG150 and PSG.
AI.motivation: Existing OV-SGG methods rely on dataset-specific object-predicate co-occurrence patterns, which under long-tailed distributions and noisy object localization produce biased, entangled relation representations that limit rare-relation recognition and generalization to unseen predicates.
AI.method: RaRe aligns rationale embeddings with textualized relation descriptions through self-supervised contrastive learning, then refines rationale generation with a specificity-oriented reinforcement learning objective that encourages object-pair-specific relational evidence, directly optimizing the rationale-derived representation space rather than using the chain of thought only as an intermediate trace.
AI.result: Experiments on VG150 and PSG show improved category-balanced recognition over existing baselines, while the additional gains from learning vary across datasets and proposal settings.
AI.conclusion: Optimizing the space of CoT rationales improves inter-relation discriminability for open-vocabulary scene graphs, though the size of the gain depends on the dataset and proposal setting.

title: Dark Matters: VAE-Aware HDR Encoding for SDR-to-HDR Video Reconstruction
summary: SDR-to-HDR reconstruction is an ill-posed problem in which clipped highlights, crushed shadows, and quantization artifacts must be recovered while preserving the original content. Latent diffusion models provide powerful generative priors for restoring missing detail, but their effectiveness is constrained by how HDR signals pass through the pretrained VAE. We find that common log-like encodings suppress low-luminance chromatic differences before generation, producing a dark-side collapse in the frozen-VAE latent. We introduce EquivFlow, a compact, invertible exposure-equivariant encoding that maps exposure changes to additive shifts while retaining a scale-independent chromatic component, without modifying the VAE. Encoding-level tests across pretrained image and video VAEs show that its exposure structure and deep-dark chroma transport persist across the tested hosts. Integrated into SDR-to-HDR video diffusion, EquivFlow delivers consistent chromatic-fidelity gains across the tested settings while retaining competitive reconstruction fidelity.

AI.tldr: Introduces EquivFlow, an invertible exposure-equivariant encoding for HDR signals that preserves deep-dark chroma in a frozen pretrained VAE latent, giving consistent chromatic-fidelity gains in SDR-to-HDR video diffusion without modifying the VAE.
AI.motivation: Latent diffusion priors for SDR-to-HDR reconstruction are constrained by how HDR signals pass through the pretrained VAE; common log-like encodings suppress low-luminance chromatic differences before generation, which causes a dark-side collapse in the frozen-VAE latent.
AI.method: EquivFlow is a compact, invertible encoding that maps exposure changes to additive shifts while retaining a scale-independent chromatic component, and it is applied without modifying the VAE; encoding-level tests cover pretrained image and video VAEs.
AI.result: Across the tested pretrained image and video VAEs, the exposure structure and deep-dark chroma transport persist; integrated into SDR-to-HDR video diffusion, EquivFlow gives consistent chromatic-fidelity gains across the tested settings while retaining competitive reconstruction fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Changing the HDR encoding rather than the VAE is an effective way to preserve chromatic detail in generative SDR-to-HDR video reconstruction.

title: Distribution Shift Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery using Machine Learning Models
comment: Accepted as a short paper at the 4th Workshop on Computer Vision for Earth Observation (CV4EO), held in conjunction with WACV 2027
summary: Remote sensing imagery acquired by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) supports wide range of applications; however, deploying machine learning (ML) models on resource-constrained aerial platforms introduces challenges beyond predictive accuracy, particularly when deployment data differ from the distributions observed during training. Such shifts are common in remote sensing due to geographic, sensor, seasonal, and other visual variations. A practical solution is to equip deployed models with mechanisms that detect emerging distribution shifts and support subsequent responsive actions. This paper presents an empirical case study of three open-source detection tools: (i) Alibi-Detect; (ii) NannyML; and (iii) PyTorch-OOD. Using cross-dataset remote-sensing shifts, we evaluate both detection effectiveness and computational latency of these tools. Our results reveal differences in detection behavior and processing cost across methods and implementations, highlighting trade-offs between detection capability and response-time. These findings motivate further work toward lightweight, and latency-aware monitoring mechanisms for resource-constrained systems.

AI.tldr: Empirically compares three open-source distribution shift detectors (Alibi-Detect, NannyML and PyTorch-OOD) on cross-dataset UAV remote sensing shifts, reporting differences in detection behavior and computational latency across methods and implementations.
AI.motivation: Models deployed on resource-constrained UAV platforms face distribution shifts from geographic, sensor, seasonal and other visual variation, so they need mechanisms that detect emerging shifts and support responsive actions.
AI.method: An empirical case study evaluates the detection effectiveness and computational latency of three open-source tools on cross-dataset remote sensing shifts.
AI.result: The tools differ in detection behavior and processing cost across methods and implementations, revealing trade-offs between detection capability and response time.
AI.conclusion: The findings motivate lightweight, latency-aware monitoring mechanisms for resource-constrained systems and further work toward them.

title: TMAL: Topology-preserving Multi-offset Affinity Learning for Curvilinear Structure Segmentation
summary: Curvilinear structures such as retinal vessels and surface cracks need both pixel-level accuracy and structural continuity. Pixel-wise supervision does not model the connections between pixels, and topology-based losses still produce ordinary masks. Connectivity-based methods predict these connections directly, but they use binary connectivity targets over a fixed local range. Such labels give the same value to thin segments and to thick regions, and they cannot describe connections at larger offsets. To address these limitations, we propose Topology-preserving Multi-offset Affinity Learning (TMAL). TMAL uses soft affinities that emphasize thin regions near the boundary, and it predicts directional affinities at several offsets to reach further. It then combines these affinities with weights that come from the decoder features, so local continuity and wider context are used together. An auxiliary segmentation branch adds region-level supervision and keeps the overlap accuracy high. On the retinal vessel dataset DRIVE and the crack inspection dataset DeepCrack, TMAL reaches the highest Dice, IoU, and clDice scores, and it greatly reduces the connected-component error $\Delta\beta_0$. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: Proposes TMAL, which predicts soft, multi-offset directional affinities weighted by decoder features together with an auxiliary segmentation branch, reaching the highest Dice, IoU and clDice on DRIVE and DeepCrack and greatly reducing the connected-component error.
AI.motivation: Pixel-wise supervision does not model connections between pixels, and existing connectivity targets are binary over a fixed local range, giving the same value to thin and thick regions and failing to describe connections at larger offsets.
AI.method: Soft affinities emphasize thin regions near the boundary, directional affinities are predicted at several offsets to reach further, these affinities are combined with weights derived from decoder features, and an auxiliary segmentation branch adds region-level supervision.
AI.result: On the retinal vessel dataset DRIVE and the crack inspection dataset DeepCrack, TMAL reaches the highest Dice, IoU and clDice scores and greatly reduces the connected-component error Δβ0.
AI.conclusion: Combining local continuity with wider context through multi-offset affinities improves topology-preserving curvilinear structure segmentation while keeping overlap accuracy high.

title: Evidential Deep Learning with conditional entropy for glaucoma detection
comment: 15 pages, 4 figures. To appear in TAAI 2026
summary: We propose a novel conditional entropy function as a basis for quantifying predictive uncertainty in Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) for glaucoma detection from retinal fundus images. Using the EyePACS-AIROGS-light-V2 and RIM-ONE-DL datasets for validation, we found that our proposed EDL model regularized by conditional entropy function produced uncertainty estimates with substantially lower calibration errors than Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout, post-hoc calibration and the conventional EDL framework based on Dempster uncertainty. To further probe our models' interpretability, we analyzed Grad-CAM heatmaps using a focus index representing spatial concentration. Compared with the other uncertainty quantification methods, EDL models exhibited greater separation between the index distributions of correctly and incorrectly classified fundus images. In particular, false negatives were associated with localized Grad-CAM activations that were displaced from the optic disc, consistent with its established clinical importance in glaucoma assessment. Overall, our findings suggest that our proposed EDL framework for glaucoma detection provides not only enhanced uncertainty calibration but also admits a more physiologically consistent interpretability.

AI.tldr: Proposes a conditional entropy function as the regularizer for Evidential Deep Learning in glaucoma detection from fundus images, giving substantially lower calibration errors than Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout, post-hoc calibration and conventional Dempster-uncertainty EDL.
AI.motivation: Uncertainty estimates for glaucoma detection from retinal fundus images need to be well calibrated and interpretable, and the methods compared against do not achieve this as well as the proposed approach.
AI.method: A novel conditional entropy function serves as the basis for quantifying predictive uncertainty in EDL; the model is validated on EyePACS-AIROGS-light-V2 and RIM-ONE-DL, and Grad-CAM heatmaps are analyzed with a focus index that represents spatial concentration.
AI.result: The proposed EDL model yields substantially lower calibration errors than Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout, post-hoc calibration and conventional Dempster-uncertainty EDL; its focus-index distributions separate correctly and incorrectly classified images more clearly, and false negatives are associated with Grad-CAM activations displaced from the optic disc.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides enhanced uncertainty calibration together with a more physiologically consistent interpretability for glaucoma detection.

title: Seeing the Small: Deformable Duality Mamba for Retinal Lesion Segmentation
summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) lesions vary widely in shape, and microaneurysms (MAs) span only a few pixels. We hypothesize that modeling the spatial organization of lesion regions, with global context and shape-adaptive scanning, improves the segmentation of such small and irregular lesions. To test this, we propose D$^2$Mamba, which couples non-causal state space duality with deformable Mamba scanning. We evaluate it with five-fold cross-validation on the DDR dataset, comparing against representative segmentation baselines under an identical training protocol, and conduct ablations on each component. D$^2$Mamba achieved the best overall performance, with 33.87% mIoU, 2.99 percentage points above the strongest baseline. The largest gain appeared on MAs, the smallest and most easily missed lesions, where Dice improved by 10.06 percentage points. These results confirm our hypothesis that spatially adaptive state space modeling benefits tiny-lesion segmentation. Code and pretrained weights are available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: Proposes D2Mamba, which couples non-causal state space duality with deformable Mamba scanning for retinal lesion segmentation, reaching 33.87% mIoU on DDR (2.99 points above the strongest baseline), with the largest gain on microaneurysms.
AI.motivation: Diabetic retinopathy lesions vary widely in shape and microaneurysms span only a few pixels, so small and irregular lesions are hypothesized to benefit from modeling lesion spatial organization with global context and shape-adaptive scanning.
AI.method: D2Mamba couples non-causal state space duality with deformable Mamba scanning and is evaluated with five-fold cross-validation on the DDR dataset under an identical training protocol, with ablations of each component.
AI.result: D2Mamba achieves the best overall performance with 33.87% mIoU, 2.99 percentage points above the strongest baseline, and the largest gain is on microaneurysms, where Dice improves by 10.06 percentage points.
AI.conclusion: Spatially adaptive state space modeling benefits tiny-lesion segmentation.

title: UniWeaver: Harnessing Unified Multimodal Models for Interleaved Text-Image Generation
summary: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) have opened up new possibilities for generating rich interleaved text-image content. However, they generally lack native support for coordinating the two modalities, and translating coarse user requests into coherent multimodal compositions also requires explicit planning. We propose UniWeaver, a structured, model-agnostic harness framework that integrates multimodal planning, generation, and visual feedback to produce coherent interleaved outputs. To train UMMs for this task, we construct UniWeaver-10K, a dataset of 10,000 tasks across 20 task families, paired with execution trajectories guided by UniWeaver. We also introduce UniWeaver-Bench, a task-oriented benchmark systematically assessing text coverage, writing quality, visual coverage, and image-text alignment. Experiments show that UniWeaver achieves state-of-the-art performance and improves interleaved text-image generation across multiple UMM backbones.

AI.tldr: Proposes UniWeaver, a model-agnostic harness that adds multimodal planning, generation and visual feedback to unified multimodal models for coherent interleaved text-image generation, with a 10,000-task training dataset and a dedicated benchmark.
AI.motivation: Unified multimodal models can generate rich content but lack native support for coordinating the text and image modalities, and turning coarse user requests into coherent multimodal compositions requires explicit planning.
AI.method: UniWeaver is a structured harness integrating multimodal planning, generation and visual feedback; UniWeaver-10K has 10,000 tasks across 20 task families paired with execution trajectories guided by UniWeaver, and UniWeaver-Bench assesses text coverage, writing quality, visual coverage and image-text alignment.
AI.result: UniWeaver achieves state-of-the-art performance and improves interleaved text-image generation across multiple unified multimodal model backbones.
AI.conclusion: Structured harnessing with planning and visual feedback is an effective, model-agnostic way to produce coherent interleaved outputs from unified multimodal models.

title: AgenticConflictLens: From Long Traffic Videos to Verifiable Conflict Evidence
summary: Traffic cameras continuously record urban road-user behavior, providing proactive safety evidence beyond crash reports. Yet safety-critical events - conflicts, near misses, unsafe turns, sudden braking, and crosswalk interactions - are rare and brief, buried in hours of routine footage. Existing traffic-video pipelines extract detections, trajectories, and risk scores but process footage uniformly, without adapting to an analyst's query. Vision-language methods improve scene understanding but often lack traffic-specific verification of participant-level conflicts. We introduce AgenticConflictLens, an agentic, query-conditioned framework for efficient, auditable conflict extraction from long fixed-camera traffic videos. Given a natural-language safety query, a Traffic-Aware Controller combines structured traffic memory with specialized conflict-analysis tools to choose where to search, which road users to examine, and which evidence to verify or reject. A coarse-to-fine search retrieves candidate intervals and applies detailed verification selectively. The framework produces conflict records with refined time intervals, participant pairs, semantic regions, trajectories, motion evidence, uncertainty, rejection reasons, and supporting clips. On 96 annotated hours from Bellevue and NYC DOT, AgenticConflictLens achieves the highest conflict-existence F1 and temporal IoU on both datasets: 0.84 F1/0.77 tIoU on Bellevue and 0.80 F1/0.73 tIoU on NYC DOT, while inspecting only 8.7% and 11.9% of video, respectively. These results support scalable, evidence-grounded urban traffic-safety analysis.

AI.tldr: AgenticConflictLens is a query-conditioned agentic framework that extracts verifiable traffic conflict evidence from long fixed-camera videos by searching coarsely, then verifying candidates selectively. On 96 annotated hours from Bellevue and NYC DOT it achieves the highest conflict-existence F1 and temporal IoU while inspecting only 8.7% and 11.9% of the video.
AI.motivation: Safety-critical traffic events are rare and brief, and existing traffic-video pipelines process footage uniformly without adapting to an analyst's query. Vision-language methods lack traffic-specific verification of participant-level conflicts.
AI.method: A Traffic-Aware Controller combines structured traffic memory with specialized conflict-analysis tools to choose where to search, which road users to examine, and which evidence to verify or reject. A coarse-to-fine search retrieves candidate intervals and applies detailed verification selectively, producing auditable conflict records with time intervals, participant pairs, trajectories, uncertainty, rejection reasons and clips.
AI.result: On Bellevue the framework reaches 0.84 F1 and 0.77 tIoU, and on NYC DOT 0.80 F1 and 0.73 tIoU, the highest conflict-existence F1 and temporal IoU on both datasets, while inspecting 8.7% and 11.9% of video respectively.
AI.conclusion: The results support scalable, evidence-grounded urban traffic-safety analysis that can be driven by natural-language safety queries.

title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
summary: As text-to-video (T2V) models are increasingly positioned as world simulators, it is essential to evaluate whether their videos conform to physical commonsense. However, existing benchmarks rely on annotators who rate each video with a single score based on intuition, yielding ratings that are subjective and do not tell which physical principle is violated. We introduce PhyRubric, a rubric-grounded diagnostic framework for evaluating physical commonsense in T2V generation. For each caption, PhyRubric constructs a caption-specific rubric before any video is seen, decomposing the caption into semantic and physical items, and derives scores from item-level verdicts grounded in timestamped evidence. We instantiate this framework as PhyRubric-Bench, which spans 34 categories across five physical domains, and scale it up to PhyRubric-Train with 3,788 videos, on which we fine-tune the open-source PhyRubric-Judge. Empirical results across ten T2V models show that physical commonsense remains far from solved, and that PhyRubric-Judge correlates more closely with human judgments than existing open-source judges while matching the frontier proprietary Gemini 4 Argon. Further analysis provides actionable insights for T2V models.

AI.tldr: PhyRubric is a rubric-grounded diagnostic framework that scores physical commonsense in text-to-video generation by checking caption-specific rubric items against timestamped evidence. It shows that physical commonsense remains far from solved for ten T2V models and that its fine-tuned open-source judge correlates better with humans than existing open-source judges.
AI.motivation: Existing T2V benchmarks rely on annotators giving a single intuitive score per video, which is subjective and does not reveal which physical principle is violated.
AI.method: For each caption a rubric is built before any video is seen, decomposing it into semantic and physical items, and scores are derived from item-level verdicts grounded in timestamped evidence. It is instantiated as PhyRubric-Bench (34 categories across five physical domains) and PhyRubric-Train (3,788 videos), used to fine-tune the open-source PhyRubric-Judge.
AI.result: Across ten T2V models physical commonsense remains far from solved. PhyRubric-Judge correlates more closely with human judgments than existing open-source judges and matches the proprietary Gemini 4 Argon.
AI.conclusion: The framework gives diagnostic, actionable feedback on which physical principles T2V models violate, and offers an open-source alternative to proprietary judges.

title: Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Astrocyte-Centric 3D Reconstruction across Normal and Stress-associated Ultrastructural States
comment: Accepted for publication in npj Imaging. 19 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables, including Supplementary Material. Code is available at this https URL
summary: The morphology of astrocytes is closely associated with their ability to support and modulate neural circuit functions; however, its reconstruction from volume electron microscopy (vEM) data remains labor-intensive and computationally resource-intensive, placing substantial barriers on its broader adoption and scalability despite the high spatial resolution of vEM. We present AstroSeg-vEM, a lightweight, astrocyte-centric framework for morphology-preserving astrocyte segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and quantitative morphological analysis in vEM images. AstroSeg-vEM combines transformer-based 2D segmentation with dedicated post-processing methods and operates directly on high-resolution EM sections, making it well suited to anisotropic vEM data and downstream proofreading workflows while preserving the full in-plane resolution of the original EM data. Across four mouse hippocampal datasets representing normal and morphologically defined stress-associated astrocyte ultrastructural states, AstroSeg-vEM demonstrates robust performance and generalization, achieving average Dice and weighted Dice values of 0.92 and 0.95, respectively, on a held-out test dataset. Its lightweight architecture enables efficient, high-fidelity reconstruction on consumer-grade hardware, providing a scalable and accessible platform for large-scale astrocyte ultrastructure analysis and future astrocyte-neuron interaction studies.

AI.tldr: AstroSeg-vEM is a lightweight, astrocyte-centric framework that performs transformer-based 2D segmentation, post-processing and 3D reconstruction of astrocytes from volume electron microscopy. It reaches average Dice of 0.92 and weighted Dice of 0.95 on a held-out test set across four mouse hippocampal datasets.
AI.motivation: Reconstructing astrocyte morphology from vEM data is labor-intensive and computationally expensive, which limits its adoption and scalability.
AI.method: The framework combines transformer-based 2D segmentation with dedicated post-processing and operates directly on high-resolution EM sections, preserving full in-plane resolution and suiting anisotropic vEM data and proofreading workflows.
AI.result: Across four mouse hippocampal datasets covering normal and stress-associated ultrastructural states, it achieves average Dice of 0.92 and weighted Dice of 0.95 on a held-out test dataset, with robust performance and generalization.
AI.conclusion: The lightweight architecture runs on consumer-grade hardware, providing an accessible platform for large-scale astrocyte ultrastructure analysis and future astrocyte-neuron interaction studies.

title: When to Start Denoising? Adaptive Denoising Entry for Generative Video Compression
summary: Generative video compression offers a promising solution for compressing and reconstructing videos under extremely low bitrate constraints, among which the diffusion-based solutions still achieve the best performance by providing the powerful generative latent prior. However, their effectiveness critically depends on when the compressed latent is introduced into the diffusion process, which directly governs the trade-off between reconstruction fidelity and perceptual realism. To address this limitation, we identify denoising start-timestep selection as a key factor governing this trade-off and formulate it as a geometric optimization problem. Based on this formulation, we propose a novel adaptive diffusion entry method for generative video compression (ADE-GVC), the first timestep-aware generative video compression framework, featuring a lightweight predictor that estimates an adaptive denoising start point from the compressed latent. A temporal adapter further extracts compression-aware conditions and injects them into a pretrained video diffusion model, enabling the reconstruction of videos with both high fidelity and realism. More importantly, we observe a strong quantitative relationship between the predicted timesteps and the distortion between the original and compressed latents, providing empirical support for our optimization formulation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ADE-GVC achieves the state-of-the-art performance on perceptual metrics and substantially improves reconstruction realism over existing generative video compression methods. Notably, our ADE-GVC achieves an average bitrate savings of 40.99\% (on DISTS) and 95.24\% (on PSNR) compared to the latest open-source baseline GLC-Video.

AI.tldr: ADE-GVC is the first timestep-aware generative video compression framework, which predicts an adaptive denoising start point from the compressed latent before entering a pretrained video diffusion model. It achieves state-of-the-art perceptual metrics and bitrate savings of 40.99% on DISTS and 95.24% on PSNR relative to GLC-Video.
AI.motivation: In diffusion-based generative video compression, the timestep at which the compressed latent enters the diffusion process governs the trade-off between fidelity and realism, and existing methods do not choose it adaptively.
AI.method: The denoising start-timestep selection is formulated as a geometric optimization problem. A lightweight predictor estimates an adaptive start point from the compressed latent, and a temporal adapter extracts compression-aware conditions and injects them into a pretrained video diffusion model.
AI.result: ADE-GVC achieves state-of-the-art performance on perceptual metrics, substantially improves reconstruction realism over existing generative video compression methods, and gives average bitrate savings of 40.99% on DISTS and 95.24% on PSNR compared with the open-source baseline GLC-Video. The predicted timesteps show a strong quantitative relationship with the latent distortion.
AI.conclusion: Selecting the denoising entry timestep adaptively is an effective way to balance fidelity and realism in generative video compression, and the observed timestep-distortion relationship supports the formulation.

title: PUMA: Probability-Constrained Sequential Interaction for Forensic Localization
summary: Image manipulation localization must jointly exploit semantic structure and noise-sensitive forensic evidence. However, the effects of spatial correspondence, matching quality, and interaction order are often conflated. Existing semantic-forensic fusion methods provide complementary representations, but do not explicitly preserve quality-mismatch information during spatial correspondence or adaptively select the order in which information is propagated across branches. We propose PUMA (Probability-constrained Unbalanced Matching and Aggregation), which combines spatially constrained unbalanced optimal transport with position-wise convex selection between two sequential operators through a shared positional interface. Before normalization, PUMA retains signed transport-mass residuals, constructs row-stochastic cross-branch and within-noise-branch operators, and updates noise features through a gated residual path. PUMA achieves strong localization results on four test sets, with scores on COVERAGE and NIST16 exceeding the published results of the representative methods listed in our comparison. The experiments support the utility of local matching states and adaptive sequential interaction for cross-source localization and several post-processing conditions.

AI.tldr: PUMA is a forensic localization method that combines spatially constrained unbalanced optimal transport with adaptive, position-wise selection between two sequential interaction orders for semantic and noise features. It achieves strong localization on four test sets, with COVERAGE and NIST16 scores above the published results of the representative methods compared.
