AI.motivation: Existing semantic-forensic fusion methods provide complementary representations but do not preserve quality-mismatch information during spatial correspondence and do not adaptively choose the order of cross-branch propagation.
AI.method: PUMA uses unbalanced optimal transport with spatial constraints and position-wise convex selection between two sequential operators through a shared positional interface. Signed transport-mass residuals are retained before normalization, row-stochastic cross-branch and within-noise-branch operators are built, and noise features are updated through a gated residual path.
AI.result: PUMA achieves strong localization on four test sets, with scores on COVERAGE and NIST16 exceeding the published results of the representative methods listed in its comparison.
AI.conclusion: The experiments support the value of local matching states and adaptive sequential interaction for cross-source localization and for several post-processing conditions.

title: FlashMotion: Ultra-Fast Long-Term 3D Motion Generation
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, 10 tables. Code: this https URL
summary: 3D human motion generation plays a crucial role in game development, extended reality (XR), digital humans, and embodied simulation. Beyond motion generation, practical pipelines include rigging, retargeting, and rendering, making ultra-fast long-term 3D motion generation without compromising quality valuable for real-time interactive applications. Despite promising progress, high-quality long-horizon motion generation under tight inference budgets remains challenging, owing to 2 coupled bottlenecks: (1) generative strategies that require many sampling steps for high-quality 3D motion generation and (2) model architectures with substantial per-step computational and memory costs for long sequences. We present FlashMotion, a co-designed framework for high-quality long-horizon 3D motion generation under a strict inference budget, covering text-to-motion, music-to-dance, and speech-to-gesture tasks. To enhance trajectory-level efficiency, we introduce a 3D motion-space MeanFlow formulation with kinematic and dynamic consistency constraints for few-step generation, together with an Adaptive Soft masking mechanism for temporally coherent motion editing. To improve per-step efficiency, we design a lightweight non-autoregressive BiMamba architecture with condition-guided state selection and AdaIN-based condition fusion mechanism, enhancing cross-modal alignment and generalization to longer motion sequences. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FlashMotion achieves overall state-of-the-art performance in both quality and efficiency across text-to-motion, speech-to-gesture, and music-to-dance generation. Code is available at FlashMotion (this https URL).

AI.tldr: FlashMotion is a co-designed framework for long-horizon 3D human motion generation under a strict inference budget, covering text-to-motion, music-to-dance and speech-to-gesture. It reports state-of-the-art quality and efficiency across these tasks.
AI.motivation: High-quality long-horizon motion generation under tight inference budgets is hard because generative strategies need many sampling steps and model architectures have high per-step cost for long sequences.
AI.method: A 3D motion-space MeanFlow formulation with kinematic and dynamic consistency constraints enables few-step generation, and an Adaptive Soft masking mechanism supports temporally coherent motion editing. A lightweight non-autoregressive BiMamba architecture with condition-guided state selection and AdaIN-based condition fusion improves per-step efficiency and generalization to longer sequences.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show FlashMotion achieves overall state-of-the-art performance in both quality and efficiency across text-to-motion, speech-to-gesture and music-to-dance generation.
AI.conclusion: Co-designing the sampling strategy and the architecture makes ultra-fast, high-quality long-term 3D motion generation practical for real-time interactive applications.

title: DepthGS: Depth-Guided Gaussian Splatting with Adaptive Regularization for High-Quality Surface Reconstruction
comment: To appear in IEEE Trans. on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
summary: Recently, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as an efficient representation for novel view synthesis, offering fast differentiable rendering and high visual fidelity, and has increasingly been extended to surface reconstruction. However, the relationship between depth information and reconstruction error remains insufficiently explored, limiting the principled design of geometric optimization strategies. To fill the above gap, we propose DepthGS, a depth-guided Gaussian splatting framework. We derive theoretical relations between depth discrepancies and reconstruction error under single-view and multi-view settings, and rigorously establish corresponding upper bounds on reconstruction error. The above analysis informs the design of adaptive regularization strategies in both single-view and multi-view optimization. More specifically, for single-view optimization, we propose a depth-difference-guided adaptive normal regularization strategy that modulates the normal constraint strength using a geometric reliability weight computed from local depth differences. For multi-view optimization, we introduce a cross-view depth consistency regularization strategy that promotes consistency between neighboring-view depth maps and the corresponding depth predictions obtained by transforming the current view's depth predictions into those neighboring views. Extensive experiments on DTU, Mip-NeRF360, and Tanks and Temples demonstrate that DepthGS achieves competitive performance in both surface reconstruction and novel view synthesis.

AI.tldr: DepthGS is a depth-guided Gaussian splatting framework that derives bounds relating depth discrepancies to reconstruction error and uses them to design adaptive regularization for surface reconstruction. It reports competitive surface reconstruction and novel view synthesis on DTU, Mip-NeRF360 and Tanks and Temples.
AI.motivation: The relationship between depth information and reconstruction error in 3D Gaussian Splatting surface reconstruction is insufficiently explored, which limits principled design of geometric optimization strategies.
AI.method: Theoretical upper bounds link depth discrepancies to reconstruction error in single-view and multi-view settings. For single-view optimization, a depth-difference-guided adaptive normal regularization modulates normal constraint strength by a geometric reliability weight. For multi-view optimization, a cross-view depth consistency regularization aligns neighboring-view depth maps with depth predictions transformed from the current view.
AI.result: DepthGS achieves competitive performance in both surface reconstruction and novel view synthesis on DTU, Mip-NeRF360 and Tanks and Temples.
AI.conclusion: Grounding regularization design in a depth-error analysis yields a principled and competitive approach to high-quality Gaussian surface reconstruction.

title: picoEmergencyNet : Attention-Enhanced Ultra-Small Deep Learning Model for Aerial Image Classification in Emergency Monitoring
comment: 6 pages, Appeared in IJCNN2026 C. Kyrkou, "picoEmergencyNet: Attention-Enhanced Ultra-Small Deep Learning Model for Aerial Image Classification in Emergency Monitoring," 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN), Maastricht, Netherlands, 2026, pp. 1-6
summary: Real-time disaster recognition from aerial imagery requires deep learning models that operate under strict memory, compute, and latency constraints. While recent approaches achieve high accuracy, their computational cost limits deployment on resource-constrained UAV platforms. This work introduces picoEmergencyNet, an ultra-lightweight convolutional neural network designed for aerial image disaster classification. The proposed architecture combines depthwise dilated convolutions with efficient channel attention and channel shuffling to enable multi-scale feature extraction at minimal computational cost. picoEmergencyNet has 23k parameters and 7M FLOPs, requiring only 0.1 MB of model storage. Evaluated on the AIDER and AIDERv2 disaster datasets, it achieves up to 96.1% accuracy, matching or exceeding state-of-the-art lightweight models that are orders of magnitude larger. Deployment experiments on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin show that, without hardware-specific optimizations, picoEmergencyNet achieves 258 FPS on GPU and 46 FPS on CPU with a 7x lower activation memory footprint compared to competing models. These results demonstrate that careful architectural specialization, rather than model scaling, enables highly efficient and accurate TinyML-ready disaster recognition for real-time UAV-based emergency monitoring.

AI.tldr: picoEmergencyNet is an ultra-lightweight CNN with 23k parameters and 7M FLOPs for real-time disaster classification of aerial images on UAVs. It reaches up to 96.1% accuracy on AIDER and AIDERv2 and runs at 258 FPS on GPU and 46 FPS on CPU on a Jetson AGX Orin.
AI.motivation: Recent disaster-recognition models are accurate but too computationally expensive for resource-constrained UAV platforms with strict memory, compute and latency limits.
AI.method: The network combines depthwise dilated convolutions with efficient channel attention and channel shuffling to extract multi-scale features at minimal computational cost.
AI.result: It achieves up to 96.1% accuracy on AIDER and AIDERv2, matching or exceeding lightweight state-of-the-art models that are orders of magnitude larger. On the Jetson AGX Orin without hardware-specific optimization it runs at 258 FPS on GPU and 46 FPS on CPU, with a 7x lower activation memory footprint than competing models, and needs only 0.1 MB of storage.
AI.conclusion: Careful architectural specialization rather than model scaling enables accurate, highly efficient TinyML-ready disaster recognition for UAV-based emergency monitoring.

title: Predicting Single-Cell Spatial Gene Expression from H&E using Pathology Foundation Models
comment: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI at Scale for Clinical Impact. Project page: this https URL
summary: Predicting gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images offers a scalable and cost-effective approach to deriving spatial molecular insights from routine histology. Pathology foundation models, typically pretrained using tile-level objectives, may not adequately capture the fine-grained cellular features required for single-cell molecular prediction. In this work, we systematically evaluate and establish domain-informed and task-specific strategies for adapting pathology foundation models to single-cell spatial gene expression prediction. Using paired H&E and Xenium 5K data, our approach improves mean gene-wise Pearson correlation by 2.67x over the standard zero-shot baseline and achieves state-of-the-art performance on this task. We demonstrate strong gene-detection performance across the full gene panel (AUROC = 0.800) and importantly identify that predictive performance varies substantially across biological contexts, with our model achieving its highest Pearson correlation for spatially variable genes (r = 0.643). Our findings demonstrate that, despite the challenges of sparse single-cell measurements, H&E-derived representations can recover biologically meaningful spatial expression patterns, highlighting both the opportunities and limitations of morphology-based molecular inference at cellular resolution.

AI.tldr: The paper systematically adapts pathology foundation models to single-cell spatial gene expression prediction from H&E images, improving mean gene-wise Pearson correlation by 2.67x over the standard zero-shot baseline. Predictive performance varies across biological contexts, with the highest correlation for spatially variable genes.
AI.motivation: Pathology foundation models are pretrained with tile-level objectives, which may not capture the fine-grained cellular features needed for single-cell molecular prediction.
AI.method: Domain-informed and task-specific strategies are evaluated and established for adapting pathology foundation models to single-cell prediction, using paired H&E and Xenium 5K data.
AI.result: The approach improves mean gene-wise Pearson correlation by 2.67x over the standard zero-shot baseline and achieves state-of-the-art performance. It reaches AUROC of 0.800 for gene detection across the full panel and Pearson r of 0.643 for spatially variable genes, its highest.
AI.conclusion: Despite sparse single-cell measurements, H&E-derived representations can recover biologically meaningful spatial expression patterns, while the limitations of morphology-based molecular inference at cellular resolution remain.

title: EgoHMP: Achieving Precise Human Motion Prediction in 3D Scenes via Egocentric Cues
summary: The complex interactive dependencies between human behavior and 3D scenes make accurately predicting human intent a major challenge for human motion prediction (HMP). While recent studies use human gaze to infer intent, gaze signals suffer from ambiguity, drift, and a reliance on eye-tracking hardware. Research in cognitive science indicates that egocentric views inherently encode potential interactions, while head motion serves as a crucial precursor in motion planning. Motivated by this, we propose EgoHMP, a novel framework that uses egocentric views and head motions as robust carriers of interaction intent. By translating this intent into an envisioning of future interactions, EgoHMP achieves precise HMP in 3D scenes. EgoHMP first employs a vision-motion alignment encoder to align the visual and motion feature spaces. Based on these aligned features, an egocentric intent predictor with a modality-aware modulation mechanism adaptively suppresses invalid interaction cues to predict an accurate interaction probability map. Furthermore, to enhance the stability and realism of the generated motions, we propose a contact-aware motion decoder. Specifically, inspired by the human cognitive process of planning trajectories prior to action execution, we first predict a global trajectory to serve as a self-prompt, effectively mitigating the optimization conflict in diffusion models. Subsequently, we introduce a multi-stage denoiser, which relieves motion artifacts by incorporating human contact modeling through a multi-stage optimization strategy. Finally, a GCN-based motion decoder is employed to synthesize physically plausible and semantically consistent motions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EgoHMP achieves state-of-the-art performance.

AI.tldr: EgoHMP predicts human motion in 3D scenes by using egocentric views and head motion as carriers of interaction intent, instead of eye gaze. It reports state-of-the-art performance on human motion prediction.
AI.motivation: Gaze-based intent inference suffers from ambiguity, drift and dependence on eye-tracking hardware, while egocentric views and head motion already encode potential interactions and precede motion planning.
AI.method: A vision-motion alignment encoder aligns visual and motion features, and an egocentric intent predictor with modality-aware modulation suppresses invalid interaction cues to output an interaction probability map. A contact-aware motion decoder first predicts a global trajectory as a self-prompt, then uses a multi-stage denoiser with human contact modeling, and a GCN-based decoder produces the motion.
AI.result: The paper reports that EgoHMP achieves state-of-the-art performance, without numeric values in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Egocentric intent cues and contact-aware, trajectory-prompted decoding yield precise and physically plausible human motion prediction in 3D scenes.

title: CJRR-Net: A Candidate-Joint Reprojection Ranking for Future-View Selection in Human Pose Estimation
comment: 10pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Accepted for oral presentation at the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA 2026)
summary: Multi-camera systems support performance recording, sports and human-movement analysis, where selecting an informative viewpoint is important for reliable human pose estimation. We propose the Candidate-Joint Reprojection Ranking Network (CJRR-Net) for future-view selection among eight calibrated cameras in MPI-INF-3DHP. The model combines current-view pose observations, camera configuration, and candidate-specific geometric features obtained by reprojecting the estimated 3D pose and its uncertainty into each candidate view. CJRR-Net achieves a selected-view 2D mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) of 105.18 pixels, compared with 114.64 pixels for the shared-input MLP and 117.56 pixels for adapted PoseErrNet. It also achieves the lowest mean error among the listed policies in each evaluated occlusion group. A blender rollout illustrates repeated camera selection. These findings support candidate-specific geometry for single-view selection in the evaluated fixed eight-camera setting.

AI.tldr: CJRR-Net selects the future camera view for single-view human pose estimation among eight calibrated cameras by reprojecting the estimated 3D pose and its uncertainty into each candidate view. It achieves a selected-view 2D MPJPE of 105.18 pixels on MPI-INF-3DHP, versus 114.64 for a shared-input MLP and 117.56 for adapted PoseErrNet.
AI.motivation: Selecting an informative viewpoint matters for reliable pose estimation in multi-camera systems, and the candidate-specific geometry of each view is not exploited by simple shared-input policies.
AI.method: The Candidate-Joint Reprojection Ranking Network combines current-view pose observations, camera configuration, and candidate-specific geometric features obtained by reprojecting the estimated 3D pose and its uncertainty into each candidate view.
AI.result: It achieves a selected-view 2D MPJPE of 105.18 pixels, compared with 114.64 for the shared-input MLP and 117.56 for adapted PoseErrNet, and the lowest mean error among the listed policies in each evaluated occlusion group.
AI.conclusion: Candidate-specific geometry supports single-view selection in the evaluated fixed eight-camera setting, and a blender rollout illustrates repeated camera selection.

title: Hint, Not Hole: Localization-Robust Video Overlay Removal
summary: Video overlay removal recovers the scene beneath burned-in subtitles, karaoke lyrics, titles, credits, logos and watermarks. Generative video models now fill a known region convincingly, but in practice the region comes from a detector or a segmenter, and it is wrong in both directions: it misses strokes, halos, whole frames and whole objects, and it covers background between characters, around boxes and on genuine scene text. Erasers that treat the mask as a hole, regenerating inside and copying outside, inherit every one of these errors. We present HintErase, which treats localization as a hint, not a hole. The model sees the full, unmasked video together with a hint channel; during training the hint is corrupted the way real localizers fail, while supervision follows the true overlay. The result is a single model that removes overlay the hint missed, keeps background the hint wrongly covered, and is trained to keep genuine scene text even when the hint lands on it. For full-length releases, a streaming pipeline handles interlaced sources, shot cuts, missed and jittering hints, paste-back and audio, with memory independent of the length of the video. This report describes the approach, the pipeline that turns it into full-length deliveries, and qualitative results; video results, with input, hint and output side by side, are on the project page.

AI.tldr: HintErase removes video overlays such as subtitles, lyrics, logos and watermarks by treating the detected mask as a hint rather than a hole, training on corrupted hints that mimic real localizer failures. A streaming pipeline extends it to full-length releases with memory independent of video length.
AI.motivation: Erasers that regenerate inside a detected mask and copy outside inherit localization errors, both missed strokes and over-covered background, and can erase genuine scene text.
AI.method: The model sees the full unmasked video together with a hint channel, and during training the hint is corrupted the way real localizers fail while supervision follows the true overlay. A streaming pipeline handles interlaced sources, shot cuts, missed and jittering hints, paste-back and audio.
AI.result: A single model removes overlay the hint missed, keeps background the hint wrongly covered, and keeps genuine scene text even when the hint lands on it. The report presents qualitative results, with video comparisons on the project page.
AI.conclusion: Treating localization as a hint makes overlay removal robust to localizer errors, and the streaming pipeline makes it usable for full-length deliveries.

title: Effects of Laser Beam Width and Measurement Noise on Tree Diameter Estimation in Laser Scanning
summary: Laser scanning has been utilized for decades to measure tree structure and geometry. Despite continuous advances in sensor technology, uncertainties arising from scanner characteristics and measurement conditions has remained relevant sources of error. In particular, factors such as laser beam diameter can introduce both systematic and random errors in the reconstructed tree geometry. This study investigates the main sources of these errors in mobile laser scanning (MLS) and quantifies their effects on stem curve (stem diameter) estimation. We discovered through simulations and experiments that the heteroscedasticity (difference in variance in ranging and scan angle) in the measurement noise is a key factor along with the beam width of the lidar, which cause the bias of the diameter estimates to depend not only on distance, but also on the tree diameter. We demonstrated that this bias can be reliably predicted and negated for trees with a diameter at the breast height greater than 10 cm using technical specifications of the sensor without any additional calibration. In experiments, the proposed bias compensation method reduced the root-mean-square error of stem diameter estimates to sub-centimeter level on boreal forest test sites. However, for small trees with diameter below 10 cm, the diameter bias becomes sensitive to the diameter of the tree$\unicode{x2013}$an unknown factor$\unicode{x2013}$and other factors, such as different bark and out-of-roundness of the stem, limiting the precision of lidar for measuring geometry of trees and applicability of the presented method.

AI.tldr: The study analyzes how laser beam width and heteroscedastic ranging noise bias stem diameter estimates in mobile laser scanning, and proposes a bias compensation that uses only sensor specifications. It brings RMSE to sub-centimeter level on boreal test sites for trees with DBH above 10 cm, but not for smaller trees.
AI.motivation: Beam diameter and measurement noise introduce systematic and random errors in reconstructed tree geometry, and their combined effect on stem diameter estimation has not been characterized.
AI.method: Simulations and experiments show that heteroscedastic measurement noise together with lidar beam width makes diameter bias depend on both distance and tree diameter. The bias is predicted from sensor technical specifications, without additional calibration, and then compensated.
AI.result: The compensation reduces the RMSE of stem diameter estimates to sub-centimeter level on boreal forest test sites for trees with DBH greater than 10 cm. For trees below 10 cm the bias is sensitive to the unknown tree diameter, bark and out-of-roundness, which limits precision and applicability.
AI.conclusion: Lidar precision for tree geometry is limited for small trees, and the presented compensation is applicable only for trees above about 10 cm DBH.

title: Exploring Synchrony for Communication in Modular Neural Networks
summary: One motivation for modular neural networks is to divide computation across components that learn distinct, reusable functions, which could then be recombined to support compositional generalisation. In practice, modular structure alone does not guarantee that such roles develop, and unrestricted communication between modules can undermine any specialisation that does emerge. This raises the question of how modular communication should be organised. The problem can be viewed as an analogue of the perceptual binding problem, where synchrony has been proposed as a mechanism for coordinating distributed representations. We introduce SyncNet, a modular architecture that separates module content from a dynamical phase state: learnt Kuramoto dynamics evolve the phases, while phase alignment determines communication through a shared channel. We evaluate SyncNet on Sort-of-CLEVR for relational reasoning and on SQOOP for systematic generalisation, where lower pair variety demands more recombination at test time. SyncNet gives the best held-out accuracy of the models compared at the three lowest pair varieties, by 5.1 percentage points at the hardest, and is competitive on Sort-of-CLEVR though below the strongest attention baselines. Test-time overrides show that performance depends on phases that evolve: fixed phases cost as much as no addressing at all, and permuting which module holds which region is nearly as damaging. A content-addressed variant trained from scratch nonetheless matches it, so the benefit appears to come from the modular decomposition rather than synchrony itself.

AI.tldr: SyncNet is a modular architecture that separates module content from a phase state evolved by learned Kuramoto dynamics, using phase alignment to gate communication between modules. It gives the best held-out accuracy at the three lowest pair varieties on SQOOP, by 5.1 percentage points at the hardest, and is competitive on Sort-of-CLEVR.
AI.motivation: Modular structure alone does not guarantee specialized roles, and unrestricted inter-module communication can undermine specialization, so the organization of modular communication needs study, drawing on the synchrony idea from the binding problem.
AI.method: Learned Kuramoto dynamics evolve phases, and phase alignment determines communication through a shared channel. The model is evaluated on Sort-of-CLEVR for relational reasoning and on SQOOP for systematic generalization, where lower pair variety demands more recombination at test time.
AI.result: SyncNet has the best held-out accuracy among compared models at the three lowest pair varieties, by 5.1 percentage points at the hardest, and is competitive on Sort-of-CLEVR though below the strongest attention baselines. Fixed phases cost as much as no addressing, and a content-addressed variant trained from scratch matches SyncNet.
AI.conclusion: The benefit appears to come from the modular decomposition rather than from synchrony itself.

title: RF3DGS: Reflection-Free 3D Gaussian Splatting with Self-Priors
comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Joint first authors: Qiang Wen, Guotao Meng, and Junhong Ruan
summary: 3D reflection removal is crucial in applications demanding high-fidelity visualization, such as museum exhibitions. In this work, we propose Reflection-Free 3D Gaussian Splatting (RF3DGS), a novel method for superior reflection removal. RF3DGS exclusively leverages a widely-adopted photometric prior for reflection removal: that the minimum pixel intensity across multi-view images corresponding to the same 3D point strongly correlates with reflection-free information. However, generalizing this principle to a 3D Gaussian Splatting within a multi-view context is non-trivial. To address this, RF3DGS first optimizes a vanilla 3DGS model using a geometric prior to estimate a coarse, reflection-free depth map for each view. Leveraging these depth maps and photometric prior, a 3D warping process aggregates reflection-free information from auxiliary views to construct a clean transmission pseudo-label for a given reference view. This pseudo-label provides a robust self-supervised signal for optimization. We further introduce an Adaptive Twin Rendering (ATR) loss to synergistically utilize this pseudo-label while preserving high-frequency details from the original, reflection-degraded images. By adeptly fusing these internal 3D self-priors with the ATR loss, RF3DGS demonstrates state-of-the-art reflection removal performance across both synthetic and real-world scenarios. Furthermore, we establish the first 3D reflection removal benchmark, based on the Unity rendering engine, for rigorous quantitative evaluation.

AI.tldr: RF3DGS removes reflections from multi-view images with Gaussian splatting by building a clean transmission pseudo-label from a photometric minimum-intensity prior and 3D warping, then optimizing with an Adaptive Twin Rendering loss. It reports state-of-the-art reflection removal on synthetic and real scenes and introduces a Unity-based 3D reflection removal benchmark.
AI.motivation: Reflection removal matters for high-fidelity visualization, but the photometric prior that the minimum intensity across views of a 3D point tracks reflection-free content is not easily extended to 3D Gaussian splatting in a multi-view setting.
AI.method: A vanilla 3DGS model is first optimized with a geometric prior to estimate coarse reflection-free depth maps. A 3D warping process aggregates reflection-free information from auxiliary views into a clean transmission pseudo-label for each reference view, which supervises optimization. An Adaptive Twin Rendering loss uses this pseudo-label while preserving high-frequency detail from the original images.
AI.result: RF3DGS shows state-of-the-art reflection removal on both synthetic and real-world scenarios, and the paper establishes the first 3D reflection removal benchmark, built on the Unity rendering engine, for quantitative evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Fusing internal 3D self-priors with the Adaptive Twin Rendering loss yields clean, high-fidelity 3D scenes without external supervision, and the new benchmark enables rigorous evaluation.

title: DisasterAgent: An Evidence-Driven Agent for Verifiable Disaster Report Generation From Remote Sensing Imagery
summary: Remote sensing disaster assessment is moving from simple damage classification toward comprehensive report-level analysis. In this setting, responders need not only damage descriptions but also verifiable evidence to guide response and recovery. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) and tool-augmented agents offer strong multimodal reasoning and perception, but they struggle to provide the evidence required for high-stakes verification. To address these limitations, we propose DisasterAgent, an evidence-driven agent that uses a Perception-Augmentation-Generation workflow to generate verifiable disaster reports from bitemporal optical imagery. DisasterAgent first invokes a specialized vision expert toolkit in the perception phase to build a Spatiotemporal Perception Graph (STPG), serving as a structured memory to store and organize disaster-induced changes across space and time. Evidence-based Augmentation (EA) then extracts evidence from the STPG, attaching inline citations that form a closed evidence loop from each statement to the supporting visual evidence. Extensive experiments on the DisasterM3 and RSCC benchmarks demonstrate that DisasterAgent consistently outperforms general-domain VLMs, remote sensing-specialized models, and existing remote sensing agents. Notably, compared with the original model, it improves the average score for disaster report generation on DisasterM3 by 13.5\% and ST5-SCS on RSCC by 15.34\%, providing a more accurate and verifiable solution for disaster emergency response. The code will be available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: DisasterAgent is an evidence-driven agent that generates verifiable disaster reports from bitemporal optical remote sensing imagery, using inline citations linking each statement to visual evidence. It outperforms general-domain VLMs, remote sensing models and existing remote sensing agents on DisasterM3 and RSCC.
AI.motivation: Responders need verifiable evidence, not only damage descriptions, but general VLMs and tool-augmented agents do not provide the evidence required for high-stakes verification.
AI.method: A Perception-Augmentation-Generation workflow first invokes a vision expert toolkit to build a Spatiotemporal Perception Graph as structured memory of disaster-induced changes. Evidence-based Augmentation then extracts evidence from this graph and attaches inline citations, forming a closed evidence loop from each statement to supporting visual evidence.
AI.result: On DisasterM3 the average report generation score improves by 13.5% over the original model, and on RSCC the ST5-SCS score improves by 15.34%. The method consistently outperforms the compared baselines on both benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The evidence-grounded design provides a more accurate and verifiable solution for disaster emergency response.

title: Marrying Capacity and Precision for Efficient 2D Gaussian Image Representation
summary: 2D Gaussian representations provide an explicit and efficient way to represent images, but their rate-distortion performance under limited budgets depends critically on how Gaussian capacity and parameter precision are allocated. Existing methods typically optimize these two resources separately, overlooking content-dependent capacity demands and heterogeneous quantization sensitivity. We present CP-GS, a capacity-precision coupled Gaussian splatting framework for budget-aware 2D Gaussian image representation that jointly optimizes capacity allocation and attribute precision under a shared rate constraint. CP-GS first constructs a content-adaptive Gaussian representation by dynamically reallocating a fixed Gaussian budget from redundant regions to areas with higher representation demand. It then introduces hierarchical distortion-aware representation quantization, using efficient rendering-based calibration to allocate precision across Gaussian attributes and further refine it within heterogeneous attribute groups. Finally, it jointly optimizes Gaussian capacity and attribute precision by constructing candidate representations with different Gaussian counts and precision configurations and selecting operating points according to decoded distortion and actual serialized size. Experiments on DIV2K and Kodak show that CP-GS achieves improved rate-distortion performance over representative 2D Gaussian and implicit neural representations across a range of budgets, while maintaining a fixed overall representation budget and low optimization cost. These results demonstrate the benefit of jointly optimizing spatial capacity and parameter precision for compact Gaussian image representation.

AI.tldr: CP-GS is a capacity-precision coupled Gaussian splatting framework for budget-aware 2D Gaussian image representation that jointly allocates Gaussian capacity and attribute precision under a shared rate constraint. It achieves better rate-distortion performance than representative 2D Gaussian and implicit neural representations on DIV2K and Kodak.
AI.motivation: Existing methods optimize Gaussian capacity and parameter precision separately, overlooking content-dependent capacity demands and heterogeneous quantization sensitivity.
AI.method: A fixed Gaussian budget is reallocated from redundant regions to areas with higher representation demand. Hierarchical distortion-aware quantization uses rendering-based calibration to allocate precision across attributes and within attribute groups. Candidate representations with different Gaussian counts and precision settings are built, and operating points are selected by decoded distortion and actual serialized size.
AI.result: CP-GS achieves improved rate-distortion performance over representative 2D Gaussian and implicit neural representations across a range of budgets on DIV2K and Kodak, while keeping the overall budget fixed and optimization cost low.
AI.conclusion: Jointly optimizing spatial capacity and parameter precision benefits compact Gaussian image representation.

title: The Target Is a Predicate: Predicate-State Grounding for Semantic-Level Video Reasoning Segmentation
summary: In this paper, we introduce Predicate-State Video Reasoning Segmentation (PS-VRS), where a query defines a dynamic predicate $P(o,t)$ over objects and time rather than a fixed object identity. Existing methods typically treat the target as permanently active once identified, leading to over-emission of masks during vacant intervals and failure to handle target switching. To address this, we construct PS-Bench, a large-scale benchmark with 2,077 videos and 16,250 queries annotated with explicit active/vacant predicate states, temporal intervals, and pixel masks. We further propose Predicate-State Grounding (PSG), a State-Bind-Emit pipeline that: (1) predicts [ACTIVE]/[VACANT] state tokens; (2) aligns them to video frames via dense cross-modal similarity; and (3) emits masks via SAM2 only for active states. Experiments show that PSG outperforms existing baselines by +9.32 J&F on PS-Bench and significantly reduces false-positive mask emissions. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of explicit predicate-state modeling for video reasoning segmentation with dynamic visual witnesses.

AI.tldr: PS-VRS reframes video reasoning segmentation so a query defines a dynamic predicate over objects and time, and PSG predicts active or vacant states before emitting masks only for active frames. It outperforms existing baselines by +9.32 J&F on the new PS-Bench, with far fewer false-positive masks.
AI.motivation: Existing methods treat the target as permanently active once identified, which over-emits masks during vacant intervals and fails when the target switches.
AI.method: PS-Bench contains 2,077 videos and 16,250 queries annotated with active or vacant predicate states, temporal intervals and pixel masks. Predicate-State Grounding is a State-Bind-Emit pipeline that predicts ACTIVE or VACANT state tokens, aligns them to frames through dense cross-modal similarity, and emits masks with SAM2 only for active states.
AI.result: PSG outperforms existing baselines by +9.32 J&F on PS-Bench and significantly reduces false-positive mask emissions.
AI.conclusion: Explicit predicate-state modeling is effective for video reasoning segmentation with dynamic visual witnesses.

title: Relaxing Cross-Modal Correspondence for Multimodal Remote Sensing Pretraining
summary: Multimodal remote sensing pretraining commonly relies on exact instance-level correspondence across modalities, implicitly treating strictly paired observations as a prerequisite for learning transferable representations. In this work, we revisit this assumption by relaxing cross-modal correspondence from the instance level to the semantic level. We introduce Semantic Pairing (SemPair), a pairing-relaxed pretraining strategy that replaces exact instance pairs with class-consistent cross-instance pairs. To characterize the effect of correspondence relaxation, we formulate a latent-factor model that separates cross-modal dependence into shared semantic structure and instance-specific correlation, showing that SemPair preserves the former while marginalizing instance-specific cross-modal correlations in expectation. We further introduce Mixed Pairing (MixPair) as a controlled interpolation between semantic and exact pairing to study correspondence granularity along a continuous spectrum. Extensive experiments consistently show that SemPair achieves transfer performance comparable to exact pairing (ExaPair), while MixPair reveals a non-monotonic relationship between downstream transfer and the instance-pairing ratio. These results demonstrate that exact instance correspondence is not a prerequisite for effective multimodal remote sensing pretraining and establish cross-modal correspondence granularity as an important design dimension for transferable multimodal representation learning. More broadly, this finding suggests a practical route toward scaling multimodal pretraining with reduced dependence on costly instance-aligned data.

AI.tldr: SemPair relaxes multimodal remote sensing pretraining from exact instance-level cross-modal pairs to class-consistent semantic pairs and achieves transfer performance comparable to exact pairing. A controlled MixPair interpolation shows a non-monotonic relation between transfer and the instance-pairing ratio.
AI.motivation: Multimodal remote sensing pretraining usually assumes strictly paired observations across modalities, which is costly to obtain at scale.
AI.method: SemPair replaces exact instance pairs with class-consistent cross-instance pairs. A latent-factor model separates cross-modal dependence into shared semantic structure and instance-specific correlation, and the analysis shows SemPair keeps the former while marginalizing the latter in expectation. MixPair interpolates between semantic and exact pairing to study correspondence granularity.
AI.result: Experiments consistently show SemPair achieves transfer performance comparable to exact pairing (ExaPair), while MixPair reveals a non-monotonic relationship between downstream transfer and the instance-pairing ratio.
AI.conclusion: Exact instance correspondence is not a prerequisite for effective multimodal remote sensing pretraining, and correspondence granularity is an important design dimension for scalable multimodal representation learning.

title: FastWild-GS: Minutes-Scale In-the-Wild Gaussian Splatting via Compact Per-Image Appearance Adaptation
summary: Internet photos of a scene differ in exposure, illumination and transient objects such as passers-by, so one set of Gaussian colours cannot explain all photos (the in-the-wild setting). Recent in-the-wild Gaussian Splatting methods mostly report hours of per-scene optimization. We present FastWild-GS, which describes each photo by a 128-dimensional Photo Appearance Token and a per-channel transform, a scale and an offset applied to the rendered image (six parameters); a small MLP predicts the colour of each Gaussian from this token and a per-Gaussian feature, replacing the spherical-harmonics colour. The same transform is applied to the renders that score Gaussians for densification and pruning, so appearance differences between photos are not counted as reconstruction error. On PhotoTourism, FastWild-GS trains in 8.8 minutes per scene with the lowest LPIPS among the compared methods, 23x faster than AsymGS, the next best in LPIPS. On NeRF-OSR, it has the best average PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS among the compared methods in 9.7 minutes per scene.

AI.tldr: FastWild-GS reconstructs in-the-wild scenes with Gaussian splatting in minutes by describing each photo with a 128-dimensional appearance token and a six-parameter per-channel transform. It trains in 8.8 minutes per scene on PhotoTourism, 23x faster than AsymGS, with the lowest LPIPS among compared methods.
AI.motivation: Internet photos differ in exposure, illumination and transient objects, and existing in-the-wild Gaussian splatting methods mostly need hours of per-scene optimization.
AI.method: Each photo is described by a 128-dimensional Photo Appearance Token and a per-channel scale and offset applied to the rendered image. A small MLP predicts each Gaussian's color from the token and a per-Gaussian feature, replacing spherical harmonics. The same transform is applied to renders used for densification and pruning, so appearance differences are not counted as reconstruction error.
AI.result: On PhotoTourism, FastWild-GS trains in 8.8 minutes per scene with the lowest LPIPS among compared methods, 23x faster than AsymGS, the next best in LPIPS. On NeRF-OSR it has the best average PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS among compared methods, at 9.7 minutes per scene.
AI.conclusion: Compact per-image appearance adaptation makes in-the-wild Gaussian splatting practical at minutes-scale training time.

title: CASCADE: Constraint-Aware SCAffolded DEcomposition for Logical Anomaly Detection
comment: Accepted at the 26th IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM 2026). 10 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables
summary: Logical Anomaly Detection (LAD) requires verifying whether all category-specific constraints, such as object counts, pairing relations, and measurement ranges, are satisfied by a query image given only a few normal references. Recent LAD methods based on Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) formulate this as checklist verification, decomposing the decision into independent textual checks. This decomposition, however, is text-only. Every item still reads the same unmodified query image, so the LVLM must extract different forms of visual evidence from one raw image. We identify this text-image mismatch as a constraint-specific perception gap, the source of two failure modes: instance conflation for binding constraints and scale drift for calibration constraints. To diagnose whether these failures stem from insufficient reasoning or insufficient perception, we compare textual reasoning guides and visual perception guides in a training-free setting. Our analysis shows that reasoning over the same image provides little benefit, whereas adapting the visual input to each constraint substantially improves verification accuracy. Based on this finding, we propose CASCADE, a training-free framework that extends checklist decomposition using constraint-specific visual scaffolds. We further introduce CASCADE++, which adapts these scaffolds at the object level by deriving their configurations from the constraint structure and reference distribution. Across MVTec-LOCO and VID-AD, CASCADE++ surpasses the full-shot state of the art by 3.9 AUROC points with only three references, and improves over the strongest VID-AD baseline by 11.4, transferring across multiple LVLM backbones without any training.

AI.tldr: CASCADE is a training-free framework that extends checklist-style LVLM logical anomaly detection with constraint-specific visual scaffolds, and CASCADE++ adapts those scaffolds per object; with only three references it surpasses full-shot state of the art on MVTec-LOCO and VID-AD.
AI.motivation: Existing LVLM checklist methods decompose logical anomaly detection into text-only checks that all read the same unmodified query image, creating a constraint-specific perception gap that causes instance conflation for binding constraints and scale drift for calibration constraints.
AI.method: A training-free comparison of textual reasoning guides and visual perception guides shows that adapting the visual input to each constraint matters more than reasoning over the same image; CASCADE adds constraint-specific visual scaffolds to checklist decomposition, and CASCADE++ derives scaffold configurations at the object level from the constraint structure and reference distribution.
AI.result: On MVTec-LOCO and VID-AD, CASCADE++ surpasses the full-shot state of the art by 3.9 AUROC points with only three references and improves over the strongest VID-AD baseline by 11.4 points, transferring across multiple LVLM backbones; reasoning over the same image gives little benefit.
AI.conclusion: Adapting the visual input to each constraint, rather than adding textual reasoning, is the key to accurate logical anomaly verification, and the gain requires no training.

title: Satellite Pretraining Is Not One Thing: A Matched-Pair Study of Generic and Earth-Observation Foundation Models for Scene Classification
comment: Accepted at the 3rd Workshop on Computer Vision for Geospatial Image Analysis (GeoCV) at WACV 2027
summary: Geospatial foundation models are pretrained on satellite and aerial imagery, but whether such an encoder beats a strong generic one for few-label land-use/land-cover mapping remains unclear, as prior comparisons rarely isolate the pretraining data. We study five matched pairs of Earth-observation (EO) and generic encoders sharing objective and architecture (DINO/SatDINO, DINOv3/DINOv3-SAT, MAE/SatMAE, MAE/Scale-MAE, CLIP/RemoteCLIP) within a benchmark of 14 frozen encoders on five RGB scene-classification datasets (0.06-30 m GSD). With native preprocessing, we evaluate k-NN, linear and attentive probes and image retrieval over six low-label splits, using paired per-image significance tests. EO pretraining is not uniformly helpful: on most datasets and metrics, it significantly improves three pairs (SatDINO, Scale-MAE, RemoteCLIP, the latter evaluated only on unseen datasets) and significantly hurts two (linear probe: DINOv3-SAT by up to 22.5 points, SatMAE by up to 8.8), with opposite outcomes even for two MAEs pretrained on the same fMoW-RGB imagery. These effects are robust to patch-token pooling and attentive probing, concentrate on small man-made objects, and are largest with 1-5% labels. Across encoders, the silhouette score of frozen embeddings predicts k-NN accuracy and retrieval mAP almost perfectly (Spearman $\rho \geq 0.96$ on four of five datasets). Pretraining on satellite imagery is thus not a reliable selection criterion; candidate checkpoints must be validated on target data.

AI.tldr: The paper compares five matched pairs of Earth-observation and generic encoders on few-label scene classification and finds that satellite pretraining is not uniformly helpful, so it is not a reliable selection criterion.
AI.motivation: Prior comparisons of geospatial foundation models with strong generic encoders rarely isolate the pretraining data, so it remains unclear whether EO pretraining beats a generic encoder for few-label land-use and land-cover mapping.
AI.method: Five matched pairs sharing objective and architecture (DINO/SatDINO, DINOv3/DINOv3-SAT, MAE/SatMAE, MAE/Scale-MAE, CLIP/RemoteCLIP) are evaluated within a benchmark of 14 frozen encoders on five RGB scene-classification datasets, using k-NN, linear and attentive probes and image retrieval over six low-label splits with paired per-image significance tests.
AI.result: EO pretraining significantly improves SatDINO, Scale-MAE and RemoteCLIP (the last only on unseen datasets) and significantly hurts DINOv3-SAT (up to 22.5 points on the linear probe) and SatMAE (up to 8.8 points); effects concentrate on small man-made objects and at 1-5% labels, and the silhouette score of frozen embeddings predicts k-NN accuracy and retrieval mAP (Spearman rho at least 0.96 on four of five datasets).
AI.conclusion: Satellite pretraining is not a reliable selection criterion, so candidate checkpoints must be validated on the target data.

title: Towards Text-Only Remote Sensing Scene Classification via Semantic Proxy
summary: Remote sensing scene classification (RSSC) is traditionally formulated as a vision-centric problem, where inference relies on rich visual representations extracted from images. In this work, we revisit this assumption by introducing text-only RSSC, a new problem setting that investigates whether remote sensing scenes can be recognized using only textual semantic representations. To enable this study, we propose SeProRS, which reformulates RSSC as a text-only classification task through semantic proxy generation. Specifically, a vision-language model (VLM) is first employed to convert remote sensing images into textual descriptions, termed semantic proxies, which are then encoded by a text embedding model for scene classification. This decoupled pipeline provides a unified and reproducible benchmark for evaluating text-only scene understanding. Furthermore, we investigate representative prompting strategies and proxy generators, and analyze their impact on classification performance, text embedding behavior, cross-generator transferability, and efficiency. Extensive experiments on three well-known RSSC datasets show that semantic proxies can preserve substantial discriminative information, while also revealing inherent limitations of purely text-based scene understanding. This paper does not aim to replace image-based RSSC, but instead establishes a new research direction by quantifying the feasibility and boundaries of semantic proxy-based scene recognition. The proposed benchmark and analysis provide a foundation for future research on efficient and modality-reduced remote sensing scene understanding. The source code and datasets will be accessible at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces text-only remote sensing scene classification, in which a VLM converts images into textual semantic proxies that a text embedding model classifies, showing that substantial discriminative information survives while revealing the limits of text-only recognition.
AI.motivation: Remote sensing scene classification is traditionally treated as a vision-centric problem, and it is unknown whether scenes can be recognized from textual semantic representations alone.
AI.method: SeProRS reformulates scene classification as a text-only task by generating semantic proxies with a VLM and encoding them with a text embedding model; the authors examine prompting strategies and proxy generators and analyse their effect on classification, embedding behaviour, cross-generator transferability and efficiency.
AI.result: On three well-known RSSC datasets, semantic proxies preserve substantial discriminative information while also exposing inherent limitations of purely text-based scene understanding; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: The work does not replace image-based classification but opens a new research direction and a reproducible benchmark that quantify the feasibility and boundaries of proxy-based, modality-reduced scene recognition.

title: Spatial-Spectral Coupling as Attention: Scaling Shape Correspondence to High-Resolution Surfaces
summary: Establishing dense correspondence between high-resolution 3D shapes remains challenging due to the spatial--spectral coupling at the core of many functional-map methods, which grows quadratically with mesh resolution. We observe that this coupling is equivalent to a scaled dot-product attention formulation, with learned descriptors serving as queries and keys and spectral basis functions as values. This connection makes efficient attention implementations directly applicable to shape matching and an effective mechanism for scaling spatial-spectral coupling. We show that optimized quadratic attention implementations can scale modern deep functional map pipelines to large mesh sizes, improving both runtime and memory consumption, while sub-quadratic methods introduce errors, particularly for non-isometric shape pairs, where an exact coupling proves most necessary. These insights motivate \textit{Geo-FlashAttention}, which restricts the exact softmax to geometry-selected surface patches and achieves near-linear empirical scaling while preserving correspondence accuracy of exact implementations. Across six standard benchmarks and three functional-map pipelines, rigorous analysis shows that efficient couplings preserve correspondence accuracy. At $60k$ vertices, these insights reduce peak training memory from 106.08 to 5.67\,GiB, with Geo-FlashAttention being $1.5\times$ faster per training step than FlashAttention. This enables end-to-end learning for correspondence problems on large meshes such as cortical surfaces, where high resolution is required to preserve disease-relevant intricacies of the surface geometry. Project page available this https URL

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the spatial-spectral coupling in functional-map shape correspondence is equivalent to scaled dot-product attention and proposes Geo-FlashAttention, which restricts the exact softmax to geometry-selected surface patches for near-linear scaling on high-resolution meshes.
AI.motivation: Dense correspondence between high-resolution 3D shapes is hard because the spatial-spectral coupling in functional-map methods grows quadratically with mesh resolution, and sub-quadratic approximations introduce errors, especially for non-isometric shape pairs.
AI.method: The coupling is recast as attention, with learned descriptors as queries and keys and spectral basis functions as values, so optimized attention implementations apply directly; Geo-FlashAttention restricts the exact softmax to geometry-selected surface patches.
AI.result: Across six standard benchmarks and three functional-map pipelines, efficient couplings preserve correspondence accuracy; at 60k vertices, peak training memory drops from 106.08 to 5.67 GiB, and Geo-FlashAttention is 1.5 times faster per training step than FlashAttention.
AI.conclusion: The attention view makes end-to-end correspondence learning on large meshes, such as cortical surfaces, practical without giving up the accuracy of exact coupling.

title: The BRIDGE dataset: paired brightfield whole-slide images of prostate core-needle biopsies in paraffin, after deparaffinization and H&E staining
summary: Computational approaches are increasingly being explored to streamline histopathology workflows, including label-free methods that aim to reduce reliance on chemical staining. Among these, deep learning-based label-free virtual staining uses images of unstained tissue to computationally generate stained images. Despite growing interest, model development and validation remain constrained by the scarcity of paired, clinically annotated whole-slide imaging datasets. We present BRIDGE, a dataset of prostate core-needle biopsies collected at the Prof. Franciszek Lukaszczyk Oncology Centre in Bydgoszcz, Poland. The dataset comprises 869 glass slides from 169 patients, each digitized sequentially after sectioning, deparaffinization, and hematoxylin and eosin staining, yielding in total 2607 whole-slide images. The dataset supports the development and external validation of label-free virtual staining, virtual unstaining, image-registration and segmentation methods. Each slide is accompanied by a Gleason score, enabling downstream analyses of cancer classification and grading concordance. The stained images can be used independently for color normalization and cross-scanner robustness studies. All images are de-identified, distributed in their native scanner format and will be available through the BioImage Archive.

AI.tldr: The paper presents BRIDGE, a dataset of 2607 whole-slide images from 869 glass slides of 169 prostate core-needle biopsy patients, each slide digitized after sectioning, deparaffinization and H&E staining and accompanied by a Gleason score; it will be released through the BioImage Archive.
AI.motivation: Model development and validation for label-free virtual staining are constrained by the scarcity of paired, clinically annotated whole-slide imaging datasets.
AI.method: Prostate core-needle biopsies from the Prof. Franciszek Lukaszczyk Oncology Centre in Bydgoszcz, Poland, were sectioned, deparaffinized and H&E stained, with each glass slide digitized sequentially; the images are de-identified and distributed in their native scanner format.
AI.result: The abstract reports no model benchmarks; it states that the dataset supports development and external validation of label-free virtual staining, virtual unstaining, image registration and segmentation, and that stained images can be used for colour normalization and cross-scanner robustness studies.
AI.conclusion: BRIDGE aims to ease the shortage of paired, clinically annotated slide data for label-free histopathology and enables analyses of cancer classification and grading concordance.

title: Region-Wise Logit Fusion and Utility-Gated Refinement for Brain Metastasis Segmentation
comment: Accepted at the Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge - Metastases (BraTS-METS), held in conjunction with MICCAI 2026
summary: BraTS-METS 2026 Task 1 evaluates segmentation of brain metastases and postoperative resection cavities on heterogeneous multiparametric MRI, requiring detection of small enhancing foci while preserving the geometry and hierarchy of enhancing tumor (ET), tumor core (TC), whole tumor (WT), and resection cavity (RC). We present COMPASS-METS (Component-Aware Multi-Trainer Probability Assembly with Structured Segmentation), which combines three five-fold nnU-Net configurations into aligned regional probability ensembles. A structured-probability anchor applies region-specific component decisions, TC boundary completion, RC filtering, and hierarchy-preserving conversion. Omitted ET candidates are recovered additively using learned component confidence and deterministic multi-trainer support for ET and its TC/WT parents; a final utility gate admits only disconnected candidates with sufficient lesion-existence and geometry-safety probabilities. On the reused 179-case challenge development cohort, COMPASS-METS (Team: MicroBT) achieved Small F1 0.354, lesion-wise DSC 0.712, NSD 0.714, All F1 0.779, and HD95 56.6 mm. Relative to ResEncXL, it improved DSC, NSD, and All F1 and reduced HD95, while Small F1 changed from 0.367 to 0.354. Stagewise analysis attributes the principal geometric gains to structured probability construction and shows that guarded ET refinement recovers most of the associated small-lesion detection loss. These 179-case results remain selection-aware development estimates. The source code is publicly available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: COMPASS-METS combines three five-fold nnU-Net configurations into regional probability ensembles with structured post-processing and guarded recovery of small enhancing tumor candidates for brain metastasis segmentation in BraTS-METS 2026 Task 1.
AI.motivation: Segmenting brain metastases and resection cavities on heterogeneous multiparametric MRI requires detecting small enhancing foci while preserving the geometry and hierarchy of the ET, TC, WT and RC regions.
AI.method: Three five-fold nnU-Net configurations are merged into aligned regional probability ensembles; a structured-probability anchor applies region-specific component decisions, TC boundary completion, RC filtering and hierarchy-preserving conversion; omitted ET candidates are recovered additively using learned component confidence and multi-trainer support, and a utility gate admits only disconnected candidates with sufficient lesion-existence and geometry-safety probabilities.
AI.result: On the 179-case challenge development cohort, the method achieved Small F1 0.354, lesion-wise DSC 0.712, NSD 0.714, All F1 0.779 and HD95 56.6 mm; relative to ResEncXL it improved DSC, NSD and All F1 and reduced HD95, while Small F1 fell from 0.367 to 0.354.
AI.conclusion: Structured probability construction accounts for the principal geometric gains and guarded ET refinement recovers most of the small-lesion detection loss, though the 179-case results remain selection-aware development estimates.

title: DroneSegEdit: Adapting Pretrained Generative Editors for UAV Segmentation with Language-Grounded Verification
summary: Recent work has shown that pretrained image generators can support diverse visual tasks. Yet directly applying them to language-guided unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) segmentation exposes a key limitation: a plausible mask may correspond to the wrong instance among small and repeated objects. We call this mismatch between mask rendering and expression-level target selection the Grounding-Rendering Gap. We present DroneSegEdit, which combines RGB proposal rendering with language-grounded, proposal-constrained verification to select supported foreground while retaining rendered geometry. DroneSegEdit adapts the open-weight LongCat-Image-Edit model using task-specific LoRA and fixed color-to-label decoding. For referring segmentation, a Language-Grounded Spatial Verifier (LGSV) reads hierarchical states from the frozen multimodal large language model backbone to derive expression-conditioned spatial evidence, which is mapped back to the rendered proposal without introducing foreground outside it. On RIS-LAD, DroneSegEdit reaches a new state of the art at 52.78 mIoU, 7.16 points above the previous best. It remains competitive overall on UAVid-RIS and VDD-RIS, with its clearest class-wise gains on compact, application-relevant categories, notably vehicles and humans. A separate verifier-free experiment extends the RGB interface to full-scene parsing: a task-specific adapter jointly renders all classes from one task-level instruction without enumerating class names or palette colors.

AI.tldr: DroneSegEdit adapts a pretrained generative image editor with LoRA and a language-grounded verifier for referring UAV segmentation, reaching 52.78 mIoU on RIS-LAD, 7.16 points above the previous best.
AI.motivation: Directly applying pretrained image generators to language-guided UAV segmentation can yield a plausible mask for the wrong instance among small, repeated objects, a mismatch the authors call the Grounding-Rendering Gap.
AI.method: RGB proposal rendering with the open-weight LongCat-Image-Edit model, adapted by task-specific LoRA and fixed color-to-label decoding; a Language-Grounded Spatial Verifier reads hierarchical states from a frozen multimodal LLM backbone to derive expression-conditioned spatial evidence, which is mapped back onto the rendered proposal without adding foreground outside it.
AI.result: On RIS-LAD it reaches 52.78 mIoU, a new state of the art 7.16 points above the previous best; it remains competitive on UAVid-RIS and VDD-RIS, with the clearest class-wise gains on vehicles and humans; a verifier-free adapter also renders all classes of full-scene parsing from one task-level instruction.
AI.conclusion: Constraining generative rendering with language-grounded verification improves instance selection in drone segmentation, and the same RGB interface extends to full-scene parsing without enumerating class names or palette colors.

title: A 10K drone image dataset with component-level annotations for rooftop photovoltaic inspection
comment: 14 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary information is included as an ancillary file
summary: Component-level information supports rooftop photovoltaic (PV) inspection, but recognizing individual components across complex scenes remains challenging. We present PVIS-10K, a dataset of 10,065 drone images with component-level annotations covering 63,632 physical PV modules across 22 rooftop installations. The high-resolution red-green-blue (RGB) images were acquired by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs, also known as drones) in Ningbo, Shaoxing and Shenzhen, China. Multi-angle oblique observations capture installation-height and scale variation, dense arrangements, occlusion, shadows and reflections. Three-dimensional delineation, reprojection and image-by-image review produced 3,516,675 image-level polygon annotations, stored in Common Objects in Context (COCO) format. Station-disjoint partitions support evaluation on unseen stations within and across cities. Four supervised models and text-prompted zero-shot Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) provide full-resolution benchmarks of instance matching and foreground coverage. PVIS-10K supports component localization, delineation and image-based counting for drone-based rooftop PV inspection research.

AI.tldr: PVIS-10K is a dataset of 10,065 drone images with component-level annotations for 63,632 rooftop PV modules across 22 installations, with COCO-format polygon annotations and benchmarks of four supervised models and zero-shot SAM 3.
AI.motivation: Component-level information supports rooftop photovoltaic inspection, but recognizing individual components across complex scenes, with installation-height variation, dense arrangements, occlusion, shadows and reflections, remains challenging.
AI.method: High-resolution RGB drone images from Ningbo, Shaoxing and Shenzhen were annotated through 3D delineation, reprojection and image-by-image review, producing 3,516,675 image-level polygon annotations in COCO format; station-disjoint partitions support evaluation on unseen stations within and across cities.
AI.result: Four supervised models and text-prompted zero-shot SAM 3 provide full-resolution benchmarks of instance matching and foreground coverage.
AI.conclusion: The dataset supports component localization, delineation and image-based counting for drone-based rooftop PV inspection research.

title: Persistent Metric-Semantic Maritime Scene Memory from Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs
summary: Three-dimensional scene graphs (3DSGs) can provide robots with persistent metric-semantic representations for spatial reasoning, but the existing methods have primarily been developed for indoor and terrestrial environments. In this paper we investigate how a representative outdoor open-vocabulary method transfers to maritime environments and which adaptations are needed. Our experiments show that zero-shot representative outdoor 3DSG descriptions agree with our labeled ground truth for a majority of geometry-supported objects on our data, but the resulting map exhibits considerable physical-entity fragmentation, and its terrestrial higher-level assumptions don't capture maritime spatial organization needs. We therefore keep the underlying mapping method and post-process its accumulated evidence. We show a metric-semantic consolidation method followed by geometry-grounded multi-view vision-language model (VLM) reasoning that reconciles remaining fragments into physical entities and groups entities through observations into local places. In parallel, we construct maritime macro regions using map priors and onboard water and structure observations, and associate them with the local places. The resulting representation reduces physical-entity fragmentation beyond both the baseline and our geometry-semantic consolidation component alone, supports correspondence of fixed local places across repeated maritime traversals, and improves contextual retrieval on our reviewed queries over tested baselines. These results show how an outdoor open-vocabulary map can be adapted into persistent maritime scene memory with our methods for object/place identity and spatial abstractions.

AI.tldr: The paper adapts an outdoor open-vocabulary 3D scene graph method to maritime scenes by post-processing its accumulated map evidence, which reduces physical-entity fragmentation and yields persistent local places and macro regions.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D scene graph methods target indoor and terrestrial environments; a representative outdoor method produces maritime maps with considerable physical-entity fragmentation, and its terrestrial higher-level assumptions do not capture maritime spatial organization.
AI.method: The underlying mapping method is kept and its evidence post-processed: metric-semantic consolidation followed by geometry-grounded multi-view VLM reasoning reconciles fragments into physical entities and groups them into local places; maritime macro regions are built from map priors and onboard water and structure observations and associated with the local places.
AI.result: The representation reduces entity fragmentation beyond both the baseline and the consolidation component alone, supports correspondence of fixed local places across repeated traversals, and improves contextual retrieval on the reviewed queries over tested baselines; zero-shot descriptions agree with labelled ground truth for a majority of geometry-supported objects.
AI.conclusion: An outdoor open-vocabulary map can be adapted into persistent maritime scene memory with object and place identity and spatial abstractions.

title: EVAThink: Evidence Sufficiency-Guided Training for Adaptive Thinking in Video Understanding
comment: The code, model, and datasets are available at \href{this https URL}{EVAThink}
summary: Under a fixed frame budget, video understanding with vision-language models (VLMs) depends on whether the sampled frames provide sufficient evidence for the question. Sufficient frame evidence supports direct answering, whereas less informative observations may benefit from reasoning that connects the available cues. We introduce EVAThink, which enhances video understanding through evidence sufficiency-guided training for adaptive thinking. First, Recoverable Evidence Gap Mining constructs evidence-dense and evidence-sparse video views that share the same question and answer under an identical frame budget. It retains pairs where sparse views yield lower direct-answer accuracy than dense views but benefit from explicit reasoning, providing supervision for response-mode selection. Second, Evidence-Guided Two-Stage Reinforcement Learning uses stage-specific rewards to guide training with evidence-based mode preferences and then refine response efficiency, while first-token advantage regularization mitigates mode collapse. Trained on only 6.7K curated samples, EVAThink consistently improves upon the base model across video understanding benchmarks under both 32- and 64-frame budgets, while outperforming strong baselines on average. The code, model, and datasets are available at \href{this https URL}{EVAThink}.

AI.tldr: EVAThink trains a VLM to choose between direct answering and explicit reasoning according to whether the sampled frames give sufficient evidence, using 6.7K curated samples, and improves on the base model under 32- and 64-frame budgets.
AI.motivation: Under a fixed frame budget, sufficient frame evidence supports direct answering, while less informative observations may benefit from reasoning that connects the available cues.
AI.method: Recoverable Evidence Gap Mining builds evidence-dense and evidence-sparse views that share the question and answer, and keeps pairs where sparse views score lower on direct answering but gain from explicit reasoning, supervising response-mode selection; two-stage reinforcement learning uses stage-specific rewards for evidence-based mode preference and then response efficiency, with first-token advantage regularization against mode collapse.
AI.result: Trained on only 6.7K curated samples, EVAThink consistently improves on the base model across video understanding benchmarks under both 32- and 64-frame budgets and outperforms strong baselines on average.
AI.conclusion: Evidence-sufficiency-guided training lets a VLM decide adaptively when to reason, improving video understanding with little data.

title: Adapting a Vision Foundation Model for Fracture Characterization in Acoustic Image Logs
summary: Natural fractures (NFs) and drilling-induced tensile fractures (DITFs) in acoustic image logs provide insights into rock mass structure and in situ stress, but manual characterization is time-consuming. Deep learning can automate this task, although expert-labeled data are scarce. We investigate whether adapting a pretrained vision foundation model (VFM) outperforms task-specific models trained from scratch with limited annotations. Using 80 annotated acoustic image samples, we fine-tuned DINOv3, pretrained on satellite imagery, and evaluated it on four boreholes excluded from fine-tuning. The adapted model estimated NF and DITF parameters comparably to human interpretation. Relative to U-Net, YOLOv8, and Swin Transformer models trained from scratch, it yielded fewer false positives and negatives and more accurate fracture counts and orientations. However, its performance advantage generally narrowed as training sample size decreased. We also assessed decoder architecture, fine-tuning strategy, and image enhancement. A progressive upsampling decoder with full fine-tuning performed best among the DINOv3 configurations tested, while fracture-focused image enhancement did not consistently improve accuracy. These results demonstrate the potential of VFM adaptation for fracture characterization in acoustic image logs with limited labeled data and suggest a transferable workflow for other annotation-scarce geoscientific imaging tasks.

AI.tldr: Fine-tuning the DINOv3 vision foundation model on 80 annotated acoustic image samples gives fracture characterization comparable to human interpretation and beats U-Net, YOLOv8 and Swin Transformer trained from scratch, although the advantage narrows as training data shrinks.
AI.motivation: Manual characterization of natural and drilling-induced fractures in acoustic image logs is time-consuming and expert-labeled data are scarce, so it is unclear whether adapting a pretrained vision foundation model beats task-specific models trained from scratch with limited annotations.
AI.method: DINOv3, pretrained on satellite imagery, is fine-tuned on 80 annotated samples and evaluated on four boreholes excluded from fine-tuning; decoder architecture, fine-tuning strategy and image enhancement are assessed, and a progressive upsampling decoder with full fine-tuning performs best among the DINOv3 configurations tested.
AI.result: The adapted model estimates NF and DITF parameters comparably to human interpretation and, relative to the scratch-trained models, yields fewer false positives and negatives and more accurate fracture counts and orientations; its advantage generally narrows as sample size decreases, and fracture-focused image enhancement does not consistently improve accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Adapting a vision foundation model offers a transferable workflow for fracture characterization and other annotation-scarce geoscientific imaging tasks.

title: MicroBT: Centroid-Guided Synergistic Learning for Multi-Modal Micro Brain Tumor Segmentation and Counting
comment: Accepted at the 37th British Machine Vision Conference (BMVC), 2026
summary: Multi-modal brain tumor segmentation is essential for clinical diagnosis, radiotherapy planning, and longitudinal monitoring. While recent studies have achieved remarkable overall segmentation performance, they rely on overlap-based objectives that inherently favor large regions, causing sub-3 mm micro-lesions to be systematically suppressed during training. Moreover, existing pixel-level segmentation frameworks lack explicit instance-level modeling, leading to unreliable lesion counting that directly impacts clinical staging and therapeutic decisions. To address these challenges, we propose MicroBT, a unified multi-modal framework for micro brain tumor segmentation and counting. Our core insight is that a fundamental geometric property is inherently scale-invariant: regardless of size, each lesion possesses a well-defined centroid. Leveraging this, we first devise a centroid-anchored synergistic paradigm that utilizes predicted centroids as shared anchors to simultaneously condition dense segmentation and instance-level localization. To counteract the tumor size imbalance, we further devise a Volume-Calibrated Loss (VC-Loss) that adaptively amplifies the gradient contribution of micro-lesions, alongside a Size-Aware Curriculum Optimization (SACO) that stabilizes multi-task training by establishing global representations before progressively unlocking fine-grained localization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MicroBT outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly on metastases, where micro-lesion ($\leq 3$ mm) localization precision improves by approximately 7% and counting estimation errors decrease by approximately 26%. The code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: MicroBT is a multi-modal framework for segmenting and counting sub-3 mm brain tumor micro-lesions, using predicted centroids as shared anchors, a Volume-Calibrated Loss and size-aware curriculum optimization.
